### `shopping_mall_customer_profiles`

Customer profile information extending basic authentication with display
name and phone number. Each customer has exactly one profile linked to
their identity in [shopping_mall_customers](#shopping_mall_customers). Profile data is
editable by the customer and changes are tracked in {@link
shopping_mall_customer_profile_snapshots} for audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`: Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `display_name`
  > Customer's public display name shown in orders, reviews, and profile
  > pages.
- `phone_number`: Customer's contact phone number for order notifications and support.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the profile was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the profile was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the profile was soft deleted, null if active.

### `shopping_mall_seller_profiles`

Seller shop profile information extending the seller actor with
business-facing details. Contains shop name, description, and logo image
that customers view. Each seller has exactly one profile (1:1
relationship). Approval status is tracked separately in
shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`
  > Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers). Unique constraint enforces 1:1
  > relationship.
- `shop_name`: Public-facing shop name displayed to customers.
- `description`: Shop description providing business details to customers.
- `logo_image_uri`: Shop logo image URL for brand identification.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the profile was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the profile was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the profile was soft deleted (null if active).

### `shopping_mall_seller_profile_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of seller profile changes preserving shop name,
description, and logo at each modification point. Used for audit trail
and dispute resolution. Each snapshot represents the complete state of a
seller profile at a specific moment in time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_seller_profile_id`: Target's [shopping_mall_seller_profiles.id](#shopping_mall_seller_profiles).
- `shop_name`: Shop name at the time of snapshot.
- `description`: Shop description at the time of snapshot.
- `logo_image_uri`: Shop logo image URL at the time of snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

### `shopping_mall_customer_profile_snapshots`

Immutable point-in-time snapshots of customer profile changes for audit
trail and data recovery. Each snapshot captures the display name and
phone number at the moment of profile modification, enabling historical
reconstruction and dispute resolution. References {@link
shopping_mall_customer_profiles} and [shopping_mall_customers](#shopping_mall_customers).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `customer_profile_id`: Customer profile's [shopping_mall_customer_profiles.id](#shopping_mall_customer_profiles).
- `display_name`: Snapshot of customer's display name at time of change.
- `phone_number`: Snapshot of customer's phone number at time of change.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the snapshot was created (when profile was modified).

cannot be modified or deleted, ensuring permanent historical record of
all address modifications.

- `postal_code`: Postal code at the time of snapshot.
- `country`: Country at the time of snapshot.
- `is_default`: Whether this address was marked as default at the time of snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

### `shopping_mall_products`

Core product listings in the shopping mall catalog. Each product
represents an item for sale with a name, description, category
classification, and base price. Products are owned by sellers who create
and manage them. Products can have multiple variants (SKUs) representing
different option combinations, multiple images for display, and maintain
an immutable snapshot history of all modifications for dispute
resolution. When deleted, products are hidden from search and category
listings but snapshots and historical order data are preserved.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `category_id`: Category's [shopping_mall_categories.id](#shopping_mall_categories).
- `name`: Product name displayed to customers.
- `description`: Detailed product description with specifications and features.
- `base_price`
  > Base price of the product in the platform's currency. Individual variants
  > may override this price.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the product was first created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the product was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the product was soft-deleted. Null if active.

### `shopping_mall_product_variants`

SKU variants representing specific option combinations for products. Each
variant has a unique SKU code, optional price override, and tracks stock
through inventory records. Variants are managed through their parent
product and can be deleted only if no pending orders exist.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`: Parent product's [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `sku_code`: Unique stock keeping unit identifier for this variant.
- `price_override`
  > Optional price that overrides the parent product's base price. Null means
  > use base price.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this variant was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this variant was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this variant was soft deleted. Null means active.

### `shopping_mall_product_option_definitions`

Configurable option type definitions for products such as Color, Size, or
Material. Each product can have multiple option definitions, and each
definition has multiple available values stored in {@link
shopping_mall_product_option_values}. Option definitions are managed
through their parent product and are deleted when the product is deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`: Parent product's [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `name`: Option type name such as 'Color', 'Size', or 'Material'.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp, null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_product_option_values`

Available values for product option definitions such as Red, Blue, Large,
Small. Each value belongs to exactly one option definition and is used to
construct product variant option combinations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_option_definition_id`
  > Parent option definition's {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_option_definitions.id}.

- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this option value was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this option value was soft deleted (null if active).

### `shopping_mall_product_variant_options`

Junction table linking product variants to their selected option values.
Each variant can have multiple option values representing its specific
configuration (e.g., Color=Red, Size=Large). This enables flexible
product option combinations without hardcoding option types.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`: Product variant's [shopping_mall_product_variants.id](#shopping_mall_product_variants).
- `shopping_mall_product_option_value_id`: Option value's [shopping_mall_product_option_values.id](#shopping_mall_product_option_values).
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp, null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_product_images`

Product images with ordering where the first image (index 0) serves as
the main thumbnail. Multiple images can be attached to each product for
display in listings and detail pages. Images are managed through the
parent product and included in product snapshots when modified.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`: Product's [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `image_url`: URL of the uploaded product image file.
- `display_order`
  > Zero-based ordering index where 0 is the main thumbnail image displayed
  > first.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this image was uploaded.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this image was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this image was soft deleted, null if active.

### `shopping_mall_product_snapshots`

Immutable audit trail preserving complete product state at each
modification point. Captures product name, description, category
assignment, and base price at the moment of change. Each snapshot is
permanently stored for dispute resolution and historical reconstruction.
Related variant states are captured in {@link
shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variants}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`: Product's [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `shopping_mall_category_id`: Category's [shopping_mall_categories.id](#shopping_mall_categories) at time of snapshot.
- `name`: Product name at time of snapshot.
- `description`: Product description at time of snapshot.
- `base_price`: Product base price at time of snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

### `shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variants`

Variant states captured within product snapshots for complete historical
reconstruction. Each record preserves the SKU code, price override, and
stock quantity of a variant at the moment the parent product snapshot was
created. Immutable audit trail for dispute resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_snapshot_id`: Parent product snapshot's [shopping_mall_product_snapshots.id](#shopping_mall_product_snapshots).
- `sku_code`: SKU code of the variant at the time of snapshot.
- `price_override`
  > Price override value at the time of snapshot. Null means base price was
  > used.
- `stock_quantity`: Stock quantity of the variant at the time of snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot variant was created.

### `shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of product variant states capturing SKU code, price
override, and option combinations at each modification point. Provides
complete audit trail for individual variant changes, enabling historical
reconstruction of variant states for dispute resolution and compliance.
Each snapshot is linked to a specific product variant and preserves the
exact configuration at the time of change.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`: Parent variant's [shopping_mall_product_variants.id](#shopping_mall_product_variants).
- `sku_code`
  > SKU code at the time of snapshot, uniquely identifying this variant
  > configuration.
- `price_override`: Price override at the time of snapshot, null if using product base price.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created, recording when the variant
  > state was captured.

### `shopping_mall_product_inventory_records`

Immutable audit trail of all stock quantity changes for product variants.
Each record captures a single stock movement with quantity_change
(positive for restocking, negative for orders or adjustments), reason
explaining the change, and timestamp. Current stock quantity is
calculated by summing all quantity_change values for a variant. Records
are automatically created on order placement, cancellation, refund, and
manual seller adjustments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_variant_id`: Product variant's [shopping_mall_product_variants.id](#shopping_mall_product_variants).
- `quantity_change`
  > Stock quantity change amount. Positive for restocking, negative for
  > orders, cancellations, or adjustments.
- `reason`
  > Reason for the inventory change such as restock, order placement, order
  > cancellation, refund, or manual adjustment.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the inventory record was created.

### `shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_options`

Junction table linking product snapshot variants to their option values,
capturing the exact option combination at the time of product snapshot.
Each record represents one option value (e.g., Color: Red) associated
with a snapshot variant. Multiple records per snapshot variant form the
complete option set (e.g., Color: Red + Size: Large). Enables
reconstruction of historical variant configurations for dispute
resolution and audit purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_id`
  > Parent snapshot variant's {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variants.id}.
- `shopping_mall_product_option_value_id`
  > Option value's [shopping_mall_product_option_values.id](#shopping_mall_product_option_values) at the time
  > of snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot variant option association was created.

### `shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshot_options`

Junction table capturing the exact option combination (e.g., Color: Red,
Size: Large) for each product variant snapshot, enabling complete
historical reconstruction of variant configurations at any point in time.
Links [shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots](#shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots) to {@link
shopping_mall_product_option_values}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_variant_snapshot_id`
  > Parent variant snapshot's {@link
  > shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id}.
- `product_option_value_id`: Option value's [shopping_mall_product_option_values.id](#shopping_mall_product_option_values).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this option association was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this option association was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this option association was soft deleted (null if active).

### `shopping_mall_carts`

before checkout. Each customer has exactly one active cart that persists
across sessions. Cart items are stored separately in {@link
shopping_mall_cart_items} with variant references and quantity tracking.

with a defined quantity and unit price captured at the time of addition.
The unique constraint on (cart_id, product_variant_id) ensures the same
variant cannot appear multiple times in a cart; instead, quantities are
combined when adding the same variant again.

checkout calculation even if the product variant's price changes later.

deleted_at.

- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this item was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this item was soft deleted (removed from cart). Null if
  > active.

shopping_mall_products} for product details, {@link
shopping_mall_product_variants} for variant information, {@link
shopping_mall_seller_profiles} for seller shop information.

### `shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options`

### `shopping_mall_shipments`

and delivery status. Each shipment can contain multiple order items from
the same seller. All items in a shipment share the same tracking
information. Customers confirm delivery per shipment, or items
auto-confirm after 14 days from shipping.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).

metadata. Append-only table for compliance and dispute resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_shipment_id`: Shipment's [shopping_mall_shipments.id](#shopping_mall_shipments).

- `actor_type`

- `actor_id`

- `old_status`

- `new_status`: New shipment status after this event.
- `metadata`
  > Additional context about the event such as carrier name, tracking number,
  > or delivery confirmation details.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this log entry was created.

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_item_id`: Target's [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items).
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`: Target's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `reason`: Customer's reason for requesting cancellation.
- `status`: Current approval status: pending, approved, or rejected.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the cancellation request was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the cancellation request was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the cancellation request was soft deleted (null if active).

### `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots capturing cancellation request state when seller
responds. Each snapshot preserves the request status, customer reason,
seller response, and timestamp for audit trail and dispute resolution.
References [shopping_mall_cancellation_requests](#shopping_mall_cancellation_requests).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_cancellation_request_id`: Cancellation request's [shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id](#shopping_mall_cancellation_requests).
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers) who responded to this
  > cancellation request.
- `status`
  > Cancellation request status at time of snapshot: pending, approved, or
  > rejected.
- `reason`: Customer's cancellation reason provided in the request.
- `response_reason`: Seller's response reason for approval or rejection. Null if pending.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

### `shopping_mall_refund_requests`

Customer refund requests for delivered order items. Customers can request
refunds within 7 days of delivery. Sellers review and approve or reject
each request with a response reason. Approved refunds restore stock
quantities via inventory records.

Each refund request is associated with exactly one order item and
initiated by the customer who placed the order. The request remains in
pending status until a seller responds with either approval or rejection.
Sellers provide a response reason explaining their decision. The {@link
shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots} table preserves immutable
snapshots of refund request state when sellers respond.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_item_id`: Order item's [shopping_mall_order_items.id](#shopping_mall_order_items).
- `customer_id`: Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `seller_id`
  > Seller's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers) who responded to this request.
  > Null if no response yet.
- `reason`: Customer's reason for requesting the refund.
- `status`: Current status: pending, approved, or rejected.
- `response_reason`
  > Seller's explanation for the approval or rejection decision. Null if
  > pending.
- `requested_at`: Timestamp when the refund request was submitted.
- `responded_at`: Timestamp when the seller responded to the request. Null if pending.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots of refund request state created when sellers respond
to refund requests. Preserves the complete state including customer's
reason, request status, seller's response, and response timestamp at the
moment of snapshot creation. Used for audit trail and dispute resolution.
Append-only and cannot be modified or deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_refund_request_id`: Parent refund request's [shopping_mall_refund_requests.id](#shopping_mall_refund_requests).
- `reason`: Customer's reason for requesting refund at time of snapshot.
- `status`: Refund request status at time of snapshot (pending, approved, rejected).
- `seller_response`
  > Seller's response text or rejection reason provided when responding to
  > the refund request.
- `responded_at`
  > Timestamp when seller responded to the refund request, creating this
  > snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot record was created.

Seller registration requests submitted for administrator review with
current approval status. Each request represents a seller's application
to gain selling privileges on the platform. Administrators review and
approve or reject requests, providing rejection reasons when applicable.

  > Timestamp when the administrator reviewed the request. Null until review

- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active records.

### `shopping_mall_seller_approval_request_snapshots`

Immutable audit trail preserving complete state of seller approval
requests at each modification point. Each snapshot captures the approval
status, rejection reason (if applicable), administrator who reviewed, and
timestamp. Used for dispute resolution and historical tracking of the
approval workflow. References {@link
shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests} as parent, {@link
shopping_mall_administrators} for reviewer, and {@link

### `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests`

Administrator promotion requests submitted by users (customers or
sellers) to gain admin access. Super administrators review and approve or
reject these requests.

Uses polymorphic ownership pattern with actor_type discriminator.
Specific actor relationships are managed through subtype tables: {@link
shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_customers} for customer
submitters and [shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers](#shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers)
for seller submitters.

Status workflow: pending (awaiting review) → approved (granted admin
access) or rejected (denied by super administrator).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_type`
  > Discriminator indicating which actor type submitted this request
  > (customer or seller). Used with subtype tables for polymorphic ownership.
- `reason`: User's written justification for requesting administrator role promotion.
- `status`
  > Current approval workflow status: pending (awaiting review), approved
  > (granted admin access), or rejected (denied by super administrator).
- `rejection_reason`
  > Explanation provided by super administrator when rejecting a request.
  > Null for pending or approved requests.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the promotion request was submitted.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the request was last modified (e.g., status changed).
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion. Null for active requests.

### `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots`

Immutable snapshots capturing the complete state of administrator
promotion requests at each status change point. Each snapshot preserves
the actor type, status, decision reason, and responding super
administrator at the moment of change, providing an audit trail for
dispute resolution and compliance. References {@link
shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_id`
  > Parent promotion request's {@link
  > shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id}.
- `responding_super_administrator_id`
  > Super administrator who made the decision's {@link
  > shopping_mall_super_administrators.id}.
- `actor_type`: Type of actor who submitted the request: customer or seller.
- `status`: Request status at snapshot time: pending, approved, or rejected.
- `reason`
  > Decision reason provided by super administrator, required for rejected
  > requests.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

### `shopping_mall_administrator_grade_changes`

Immutable audit trail of administrator grade changes when super
administrators promote or demote other administrators. Records
transitions between regular administrator and super administrator grades
for accountability and system oversight.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_administrator_id`
  > The administrator whose grade was changed. {@link
  > shopping_mall_administrators.id}.
- `shopping_mall_super_administrator_id`
  > The super administrator who performed the grade change. {@link
  > shopping_mall_super_administrators.id}.
- `previous_grade`
  > The administrator's grade before the change: 'administrator' or
  > 'super_administrator'.
- `new_grade`
  > The administrator's grade after the change: 'administrator' or
  > 'super_administrator'.
- `reason`: Optional reason or note for the grade change.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the grade change was recorded.

### `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_customers`

Subtype table linking administrator promotion requests to customer
actors. Implements polymorphic ownership pattern where the main
admin_promotion_requests table holds common fields and this table
provides the customer-specific foreign key relationship. Each promotion
request is linked to exactly one customer actor.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_id`
  > Parent's [shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id](#shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests). Unique
  > constraint ensures 1:1 relationship.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`
  > Customer's [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers). The customer who submitted
  > the promotion request.
- `shopping_mall_customer_session_id`
  > Customer session's [shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id](#shopping_mall_customer_sessions). Audit
  > trail of which session was used to submit the request.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the subtype record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the subtype record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft delete. Null if active.

### `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers`

Subtype table linking administrator promotion requests to seller actors.
Implements polymorphic ownership pattern where each promotion request is
associated with exactly one seller. The unique constraint on
shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_id enforces 1:1 relationship,
ensuring a request cannot be linked to multiple sellers.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_id`
  > Target's [shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id](#shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests). Unique
  > foreign key enforcing 1:1 relationship between promotion request and
  > seller.
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`
  > Target's [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers). The seller who submitted the
  > promotion request.
- `shopping_mall_seller_session_id`
  > Target's [shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id](#shopping_mall_seller_sessions). The seller session
  > used when submitting the request, for audit purposes.

instruction:
## Customer Account APIs
- Customer signup with email and password
- Customer login with email and password
- Customer change password
- Customer delete account

## Customer Profile APIs
- Get customer profile (display name, phone number)
- Update customer profile (display name, phone number)

## Address Management APIs
- Get list of customer's addresses
- Add new address (recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state/province, postal code, country)
- Update address
- Delete address
- Set default address

## Seller Account APIs
- Seller signup with email and password
- Seller login with email and password
- Seller change password
- Get seller approval status (pending, approved, rejected)
- Get rejection reason if rejected
- Submit new seller registration request (for rejected sellers)
- Delete seller account (with validation: no pending orders, no pending cancellation/refund requests)

## Seller Profile APIs
- Get seller profile (shop name, shop description, logo image)
- Update seller profile (shop name, description, logo)
- View seller profiles (for customers)

## Category APIs
- Get list of all categories (with subcategories)
- Get products within a category
- Admin: Create category/subcategory
- Admin: Update category name and description
- Admin: Delete category

## Product APIs
- Seller: Create product (name, description, category, base price)
- Seller: Get own products
- Seller: Update product
- Seller: Delete product (with validation: no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund requests)
- Seller: Get product snapshots
- Admin: Get all products
- Admin: Get product snapshots
- Admin: Delete any product
- Customer: Search products by name (paginated)
- Customer: Filter search by category, price range, in-stock only
- Customer: Sort search by newest, price low-high, price high-low
- Customer: Get product detail (all images, name, description, category, seller info, variants, ratings, reviews)
- Customer: Get product listing (main image, name, price/price range, seller shop name, average rating)

## Product Image APIs
- Seller: Upload multiple images for product
- Seller: Reorder images (set first as thumbnail)
- Seller: Delete image from product

## Product Variant (SKU) APIs
- Seller: Add variant to product (SKU code, option values, price, stock quantity)
- Seller: Update variant (SKU code, option values, price)
- Seller: Delete variant (with validation: no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund requests)
- Seller: Get variant snapshots

## Inventory Management APIs
- Seller: Add inventory (restock) with quantity and reason
- Seller: Subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with quantity and reason
- Seller: Get inventory history for variant
- Get current stock quantity (calculated from inventory records)

## Wishlist APIs
- Customer: Add product to wishlist
- Customer: Get wishlist (paginated, shows products not variants)
- Customer: Remove product from wishlist

## Shopping Cart APIs
- Customer: Add variant to cart (with quantity, combines if same variant exists)
- Customer: Get cart (shows product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal, total)
- Customer: Update cart item quantity
- Customer: Remove item from cart
- Cart shows stock warnings and unavailable items

## Checkout APIs
- Customer: Get order review summary (items with prices, shipping address, total)
- Customer: Place order (processes payment, creates order)

## Payment APIs
- Process payment (succeed or fail)
- If payment fails, order not created
- If payment succeeds, order created

## Order APIs
- Customer: Get order history (paginated, sorted by newest, shows order number, date, total, status)
- Customer: Get order details (items with product name, variant, quantity, price, status; shipping address; shipments with tracking)
- Seller: Get order items for their products
- Seller: Filter order items by status
- Admin: Get all orders
- Admin: Force-cancel items or entire order
- Admin: Force-refund items or entire order

## Shipping and Tracking APIs
- Seller: Get order items needing shipping
- Seller: Create shipment (select items, enter carrier name and tracking number)
- Customer: Get tracking information for shipment
- Customer: Confirm delivery for shipment

## Order Cancellation APIs
- Customer: Request cancellation for order item (status "paid" only, with reason)
- Seller: Get cancellation requests
- Seller: Approve cancellation request
- Seller: Reject cancellation request
- Get cancellation request snapshots

## Refund Request APIs
- Customer: Request refund for order item (status "delivered" only, within 7 days, with reason)
- Seller: Get refund requests
- Seller: Approve refund request
- Seller: Reject refund request
- Get refund request snapshots

## Review APIs
- Customer: Create review for delivered product (rating 1-5, optional text, one per product per order)
- Customer: Get reviews for product (sorted by newest)
- Customer: Update own review
- Customer: Delete own review
- Get review snapshots
- Get product average rating

## Seller Dashboard APIs
- Seller: Get shop summary (total products, total order items, pending cancellation requests, pending refund requests)
- Seller: Get all order items for their products (filterable by status)

## Administrator APIs
- User: Request to become administrator (with reason)
- Super Admin: Get pending admin requests
- Super Admin: Approve admin request
- Super Admin: Reject admin request
- Super Admin: Promote regular admin to super admin
- Super Admin: Demote other super admin to regular admin
- Admin: Get pending seller approvals
- Admin: Approve seller registration
- Admin: Reject seller registration (with reason)
- Admin: Suspend seller account
- Admin: Unsuspend seller account
- Admin: Get all customers
- Admin: Ban customer
- Admin: Unban customer
- Admin: Get all sellers
- Admin: Ban seller

operations.specification: Register new customer account with email and password. Validate email uniqueness and password strength. Create customer record with hashed password. Generate email verification token and send verification email. Return JWT tokens for immediate authentication. Email verification can be completed later via verifyEmail endpoint.
operations.description:
Creates a new customer account in the shopping mall system. The endpoint accepts email and password credentials, validates that the email is not already registered, and ensures the password meets security requirements.

Upon successful registration, the system creates a customer record in the shopping_mall_customers table with a bcrypt hashed password. An email verification token is automatically generated and stored in shopping_mall_customer_email_verifications table with an expiration timestamp. The customer receives JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate system access.

The customer should verify their email address using the verifyEmail endpoint with the token sent to their email. Unverified accounts may have limited functionality depending on business rules.

requestBody.description: Customer registration credentials including email and password for account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and customer information upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate customer with email and password. Validate credentials against shopping_mall_customers table. Verify account is not deleted. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in shopping_mall_customer_sessions with client information (ip, href, referrer) and expiration timestamp. Return tokens and customer info.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing customer using their email and password credentials. The endpoint validates the provided credentials against the shopping_mall_customers table, verifying the password hash matches and the account is active (not soft deleted).

Upon successful authentication, the system generates a new JWT access token and refresh token pair. A session record is created in the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, capturing the client's IP address, application URL, and referrer information along with the session expiration timestamp.

The response includes the JWT tokens for API authentication and basic customer information. The access token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent API requests. The refresh token is used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials with email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and customer information upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh JWT access token using valid refresh token. Validate refresh token against shopping_mall_customer_sessions table. Check session is not expired (expired_at). Verify customer account is still active. Generate new access and refresh token pair. Update session record with new tokens and expiration. Return new tokens.
operations.description:
Renews the customer's authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. This endpoint allows customers to obtain new access tokens without re-entering their credentials when the current access token expires.

The system validates the provided refresh token against the shopping_mall_customer_sessions table, ensuring the session exists and has not passed its expiration timestamp (expired_at). The customer account is also verified to be active and not soft deleted.

Upon successful validation, a new JWT access token and refresh token pair is generated. The session record is updated with the new tokens and a fresh expiration timestamp. The old refresh token becomes invalid, implementing a rotating refresh token strategy for enhanced security.

This operation enables seamless continued authentication for customers with valid sessions while maintaining security through token rotation.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new access token without re-authentication.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens upon successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Register a new seller account with email and password. Creates a record in shopping_mall_sellers table with bcrypt hashed password. Generates an email verification token in shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications table and sends verification email. Returns JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration. The seller account is created but requires administrator approval via shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests before gaining selling privileges. Email must be unique across all sellers. Password must meet security requirements (minimum length, complexity). Implementation: 1) Validate email format and uniqueness, 2) Validate password strength, 3) Hash password with bcrypt, 4) Insert seller record, 5) Generate verification token with expiration, 6) Insert email verification record, 7) Generate JWT tokens, 8) Create session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions, 9) Return tokens with seller ID.
operations.description:
Register a new seller account on the shopping mall platform. This operation creates a seller identity with email and password authentication credentials in the shopping_mall_sellers table.

Upon successful registration, the system generates an email verification token stored in shopping_mall_seller_email_verifications and sends a verification email to the provided address. The seller must verify their email before the account becomes fully active.

The registration returns JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication. However, the seller account requires administrator approval through the seller approval workflow (shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests) before gaining privileges to list products and manage inventory.

Email addresses must be unique across all seller accounts. Passwords are hashed using bcrypt before storage. The operation validates email format, password strength requirements, and checks for existing accounts.

requestBody.description: Seller registration credentials including email for authentication and communication, and password for account security.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and seller identity information upon successful registration. Contains JWT access token, refresh token, token expiration timestamp, and seller ID for session management.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate seller with email and password credentials. Validates credentials against shopping_mall_sellers table by comparing provided password with stored bcrypt password_hash. On successful authentication, creates a session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions table with IP address, href, referrer, and expiration timestamp. Returns JWT access and refresh tokens. Implementation: 1) Find seller by email, 2) Verify password against password_hash using bcrypt comparison, 3) Check account is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null), 4) Generate JWT access and refresh tokens, 5) Create session record with client metadata, 6) Return tokens with seller ID and session expiration.
operations.description:
Authenticate a seller account using email and password credentials. This operation validates the provided credentials against the shopping_mall_sellers table.

The system verifies the password by comparing it with the stored bcrypt password_hash. Upon successful authentication, JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned to the client.

A session record is created in shopping_mall_seller_sessions table containing the seller ID, client IP address, page URL (href), referrer URL, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. This session tracking enables security monitoring and session management.

The operation returns an error if the email does not exist, the password is incorrect, or the account has been soft deleted. Successful login provides immediate access to seller dashboard and management features, though product listing privileges require administrator approval status.

requestBody.description: Seller authentication credentials including registered email address and password for identity verification.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and seller identity information upon successful login. Contains JWT access token, refresh token, token expiration timestamp, and seller ID for session management.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh JWT access token using a valid refresh token. Validates the refresh token against active sessions in shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. Checks session has not expired (expired_at is in the future) and seller account is still active (deleted_at is null). Generates new access and refresh token pair. Implementation: 1) Validate refresh token signature and extract seller ID, 2) Query shopping_mall_seller_sessions for matching session, 3) Verify session expired_at is in the future, 4) Verify seller deleted_at is null, 5) Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens, 6) Update session expired_at timestamp, 7) Return new token pair.
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. This operation extends the seller's authenticated session without requiring re-entry of credentials.

The system validates the provided refresh token against active sessions in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. The session must not have expired (expired_at timestamp must be in the future) and the seller account must remain active (deleted_at must be null).

Upon successful validation, a new JWT access token and refresh token pair is generated. The session record's expiration timestamp is updated to extend the session lifetime.

This operation enables seamless continued access to seller features without interrupting the user experience. Refresh tokens should be rotated on each use for enhanced security. The operation returns an error if the refresh token is invalid, expired, or the associated account has been deleted.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authentication tokens. The token must be valid and associated with an active seller session.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens and seller identity information. Contains fresh JWT access token, refresh token, token expiration timestamp, and seller ID for continued session management.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Create new administrator account with email and password. Validate email uniqueness against existing administrators. Hash password using bcrypt before storing. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful registration. Return tokens in response. Reject if email already exists or validation fails.
operations.description:
Register a new administrator account for the shopping mall system. This endpoint creates an administrator account with the provided email and password credentials.

The email address must be unique across all administrator accounts. The password will be securely hashed using bcrypt before storage. Upon successful registration, the system generates JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication.

Administrators manage seller approvals, categories, products, orders, and user accounts within the shopping mall platform. This operation establishes the initial credentials for administrator access.

Returns authentication tokens on success. Fails with conflict error if the email address is already registered to an existing administrator account.

requestBody.description: Administrator registration credentials including email and password for account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens granting administrator access to the system.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate administrator credentials and issue JWT tokens. Validate email exists in shopping_mall_administrators table and password matches stored hash. Generate new access and refresh tokens on successful authentication. Return tokens with administrator profile information. Reject invalid credentials with authentication error.
operations.description:
Authenticate an administrator and issue JWT access and refresh tokens. This endpoint validates the provided email and password credentials against the administrator account database.

The system verifies the email address exists in the shopping_mall_administrators table and the provided password matches the stored bcrypt hash. Upon successful authentication, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned.

Administrators use these tokens to access management endpoints for seller approvals, categories, products, orders, and user accounts. The access token grants immediate API access while the refresh token enables token renewal without re-authentication.

Returns authentication tokens on success. Fails with unauthorized error if credentials are invalid or the account is soft deleted.

requestBody.description: Administrator login credentials with email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens granting administrator access to the system.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh JWT access token using valid refresh token. Validate refresh token exists in shopping_mall_administrator_sessions table and has not expired. Generate new access and refresh token pair. Return new tokens in response. Invalidate old refresh token. Reject expired or invalid tokens.
operations.description:
Renew administrator authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. This endpoint enables token refresh without requiring re-authentication with email and password credentials.

The system validates the provided refresh token against the shopping_mall_administrator_sessions table, checking that it exists, has not expired, and belongs to an active administrator account. Upon successful validation, a new access and refresh token pair is generated.

The old refresh token is invalidated to prevent reuse, ensuring token rotation security. This operation maintains continuous administrator session access while implementing secure token lifecycle management.

Returns new authentication tokens on success. Fails with unauthorized error if the refresh token is expired, invalid, or the administrator account has been deleted.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new administrator authentication tokens.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens granting administrator access to the system.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Register a new super administrator account. Validate email format and uniqueness against existing accounts. Hash the password using bcrypt before storing. Create the account record with current timestamp. Generate initial JWT access and refresh tokens. Store session information including IP address and client details. Return tokens and account information to the client.
operations.description:
Register a new super administrator account in the system. This endpoint creates a super administrator account with email and password authentication credentials.

The email address must be unique across all super administrator accounts and will be used for login. The password is hashed using bcrypt before storage for security. Upon successful registration, the system generates JWT access and refresh tokens for immediate authentication.

This operation creates a session record in shopping_mall_super_administrator_sessions table, storing the access token, refresh token, client IP address, and session metadata. The account is immediately active upon registration.

Email validation ensures proper format. Password requirements should meet security standards. Duplicate email addresses will be rejected with a conflict error.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials for new super administrator account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and account information for newly registered super administrator.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate super administrator credentials. Validate email exists and is not soft deleted. Verify password hash matches provided password. Generate new JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record with client metadata. Return tokens and account information.
operations.description:
Authenticate a super administrator using email and password credentials. This endpoint validates the provided credentials and issues JWT tokens for API access.

The system verifies the email address exists in the shopping_mall_super_administrators table and that the account is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). The provided password is compared against the stored bcrypt password hash.

Upon successful authentication, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and stored in the shopping_mall_super_administrator_sessions table along with client metadata including IP address, request URL, and referrer. The session expiration is set according to system configuration.

Invalid credentials return an authentication error. Soft deleted accounts cannot login. Multiple failed login attempts may trigger security measures.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for super administrator authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and account information for authenticated super administrator.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh JWT access token using valid refresh token. Validate refresh token exists in session table and is not expired. Verify the associated account exists and is not soft deleted. Generate new access and refresh tokens. Update session record with new tokens. Return new token pair.
operations.description:
Refresh authentication tokens for an authenticated super administrator session. This endpoint allows clients to obtain new JWT tokens using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication.

The system validates the provided refresh token against the shopping_mall_super_administrator_sessions table, ensuring the token exists, matches an active session, and has not expired. The associated super administrator account is verified to exist and not be soft deleted.

Upon successful validation, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated. The session record is updated with the new tokens, maintaining the same session metadata. The old refresh token is invalidated and replaced.

Expired refresh tokens return an authentication error. Deleted or suspended accounts cannot refresh tokens. Clients should use this endpoint before the access token expires to maintain continuous authentication.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authentication tokens.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens for continued super administrator session.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Register new customer account with email and password. Validate email uniqueness and password strength. Create customer record with hashed password. Generate email verification token and send verification email. Return JWT tokens for immediate authentication. Email verification can be completed later via verifyEmail endpoint.
operations.description:
Creates a new customer account in the shopping mall system. The endpoint accepts email and password credentials, validates that the email is not already registered, and ensures the password meets security requirements.

Create a new shipping address for the authenticated customer.

This operation allows customers to add shipping addresses to their account for order delivery. Each address must include complete information: recipient name, phone number, street address, city, state or province, postal code, and country.

Customers can maintain multiple addresses for different delivery locations such as home, work, or family addresses. One address can be designated as the default shipping address, which is used automatically during checkout unless the customer selects a different address.

Each address is associated with the customer who created it and is not visible to other customers. Address information is preserved with orders even if the original address is later modified or deleted from the customer's address book.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new address record in shopping_mall_addresses table.

Validate all required fields are present and non-empty: recipient_name, recipient_phone, street_address, city, state, postal_code, country. Validate phone number format for the specified country.

Set shopping_mall_customer_id from authenticated customer's session token. Generate UUID for id field. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp. Set deleted_at to null. Set is_default based on request (defaults to false if not specified).

If is_default is true, update any existing default address for this customer to is_default=false before inserting the new address to maintain the unique constraint on [shopping_mall_customer_id, is_default].

Return the created address entity with all fields including generated id and timestamps.

All fields are required and must contain valid values.

The address must belong to the authenticated customer and must not be soft-deleted. If updating the default address designation to true, the system ensures only one address per customer can be marked as default. The updated address is returned with all current field values including timestamps.

Verify all required fields are provided in request body: recipient_name, recipient_phone, street_address, city, state, postal_code, country. If is_default is being set to true, ensure no other address for this customer has is_default=true (or atomically unset others). Update the address record with new values and set updated_at to current timestamp. Return the complete updated address entity. Reject with 404 if address not found or doesn't belong to customer. Reject with 400 if any required field is missing or invalid.

operations.description:
Soft-delete a saved shipping address from the customer's address book.

This operation allows customers to remove addresses they no longer need by marking them as deleted. The address must belong to the authenticated customer and cannot be currently designated as their default shipping address. If the address is set as default, the customer must first designate a different address as default before deletion is allowed.

The address is soft-deleted by setting a deletion timestamp, hiding it from the customer's active address list. The record remains in the database for audit purposes and is not permanently removed.

Deleting an address does not affect past orders that used this address for shipping. Order records preserve a snapshot of the shipping address at the time of purchase, ensuring order history remains complete and accurate even after the original address is deleted from the customer's address book.

The operation validates that the address exists and belongs to the requesting customer. Attempts to delete non-existent addresses or addresses belonging to other customers are rejected.

3. Check is_default flag - if true, reject with error requiring customer to change default first
4. Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at timestamp to current time
5. Return null on successful deletion

Edge cases:
- Address not found: return 404
- Address belongs to different customer: return 403
- Address is default: return 400 with message to change default first
- Already deleted: return 404

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product categories.

This operation provides category browsing capabilities for customers and category management views for administrators. Supports filtering by parent category to retrieve subcategories, text search by category name, and configurable pagination.

Categories are organized in a one-level hierarchy: top-level categories have no parent, while subcategories reference a parent category. When viewing a category, customers see all products assigned to that category and its subcategories.

Only administrators can create, edit, or delete categories. All authenticated users can browse the category list for product discovery.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_categories table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply filters:
- parent_id: filter by parent category (null for top-level categories, UUID for subcategories)
- search: partial match on category name
- deleted_at: exclude soft-deleted categories for non-admin users

Support cursor-based pagination with configurable page size and sorting options (created_at, name, updated_at).

Return category summaries including id, name, description, parent_id, and hasChildren flag for UI tree rendering.

Authorization: Allow customer and administrator roles. Exclude soft-deleted categories from customer results.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific category by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete category information including the category name, description, parent category reference (if it's a subcategory), and timestamps. Customers use this endpoint to view category details when navigating the product catalog. Administrators use it when managing the category structure.

The response includes the parent_id field which indicates whether this is a top-level category (null) or a subcategory (references parent category ID). This enables clients to reconstruct the category hierarchy for navigation purposes.

Note: Soft-deleted categories (deleted_at is not null) are not accessible through this endpoint. To access soft-deleted categories for recovery purposes, administrators should use the category management endpoints.
operations.name: at

Query shopping_mall_categories table by the provided categoryId UUID parameter.

Return the full category entity including id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields.

Create a new product category or subcategory in the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows administrators to establish new categories for organizing products. Administrators can create top-level categories by omitting the parent_id, or create subcategories by specifying an existing category's ID as the parent. The category structure supports one level of nesting only - subcategories cannot have their own subcategories.

Both name and description are required fields. Category names must be unique among sibling categories (categories sharing the same parent). This operation is restricted to administrators only; customers and sellers cannot create categories.

operations.specification: Insert a new record into shopping_mall_categories table with the provided name, description, and optional parent_id. Generate a UUID for the id field. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp. Validate that the category name is unique among siblings (same parent_id). If parent_id is provided, verify the parent category exists and is not itself a subcategory (enforce one-level nesting). Return the complete created category entity including all fields.

Update an existing product category's name and description.

This operation allows administrators to modify category information to keep the product classification system accurate and relevant. Only the name and description fields can be updated; the category's hierarchical position (whether it is a top-level category or subcategory) cannot be changed after creation.

The updated category is returned in the response. Category names must remain unique among sibling categories (categories sharing the same parent). Attempts to create duplicate names within the same parent category will be rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update shopping_mall_categories record by categoryId UUID.

Validate requester has administrator role authorization.
Verify category exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null).
Validate name and description are provided and non-empty.
Check name uniqueness among sibling categories (same parent_id).
Ensure parent_id is not modified (hierarchical position locked after creation).
Update name and description fields, set updated_at to current timestamp.
Return updated IShoppingMallCategory entity.

Handle errors: 404 if category not found, 400 if validation fails (duplicate name, missing fields), 403 if not administrator.
