operations.description:
Permanently remove a category from the platform's classification system.

This operation deletes a category and all its subcategories if it is a parent category. Products that were assigned to the deleted category or its subcategories become uncategorized but remain accessible through search and direct links. The deletion uses soft delete mechanism, marking the category with a deleted_at timestamp.

Only administrators can perform this operation. Customers and sellers attempting to delete categories will receive an access denied response. Before deletion, verify the category exists and is not already deleted.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete category by UUID with cascade to subcategories.

1. Verify caller is administrator (authorization middleware)
2. Query shopping_mall_categories WHERE id = {categoryId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. If not found, return 404 Not Found
4. Begin transaction
5. If category has children (subcategories), recursively soft-delete all descendants by setting deleted_at = NOW()
6. Soft-delete the target category by setting deleted_at = NOW()
7. Commit transaction
8. Return 204 No Content (no response body)

Note: Products referencing this category are NOT deleted or modified. They become uncategorized (parent_id remains but category is deleted). Cascade delete applies only to subcategories via the recursive relation onDelete: Cascade.

operations.description:
Retrieve historical snapshots of a specific category for audit and historical reconstruction purposes.

This operation returns a paginated list of all snapshots created for the specified category. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the category at a point in time, including the category name, description, and parent category relationship as they existed when the snapshot was created.

Category snapshots are automatically created whenever a category is modified and are preserved immutably. They cannot be modified or deleted. This endpoint is accessible to administrators who manage categories and need to track changes over time.

Supports filtering by date range and sorting options to facilitate reviewing changes over specific time periods.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_category_snapshots table filtering by shopping_mall_category_id matching the categoryId path parameter.

Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based pagination support. Default sort by created_at descending (newest first).

Support optional filtering in request body: createdAfter, createdBefore date range filters, and sortBy options (created_at asc/desc).

Return snapshot summary information including id, name, description, parent_id, and created_at. Do not include relation data - snapshots are standalone historical records.

Validate that the categoryId exists in shopping_mall_categories table before querying snapshots. Return 404 if category not found.

Authorization: Require administrator role. Regular customers and sellers cannot access category snapshots.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of category snapshot summaries

requestBody.description: Optional filtering and pagination parameters for snapshot search

prerequisites.description: Category must be created before snapshots can exist, as snapshots are immutable audit records that reference the parent category via foreign key

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific category snapshot by its unique identifier.

This operation returns an immutable snapshot record that captures the complete state of a category at a specific point in time. Snapshots include the category name, description, and parent category relationship as they existed when the snapshot was created.

Category snapshots are automatically created by the system whenever a category is modified, providing an audit trail for historical reconstruction and dispute resolution. Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted once created.

Administrators can view snapshots of any category. Sellers and customers do not have access to category snapshots as categories are administrator-managed entities.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_category_snapshots table by snapshotId.

Validate that the snapshot's shopping_mall_category_id matches the provided categoryId parameter to ensure referential integrity and prevent unauthorized access.

Verify administrator authorization before returning the snapshot.

Return the complete snapshot record including id, shopping_mall_category_id, name, description, parent_id, and created_at.

Return 404 if snapshot not found or if snapshot does not belong to the specified category.

responseBody.description: Complete category snapshot record with historical state

parameters.description: Category ID (scope validator - snapshot must belong to this category)
parameters.name: categoryId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of active products from the shopping mall catalog.

This operation provides comprehensive product search capabilities including partial name matching, category filtering, price range filtering, and in-stock availability filtering. Results support multiple sorting options including newest first, price ascending, and price descending.

Only active products (not deleted by sellers) are included in search results. Each result includes essential product information optimized for listing displays: main image, name, price or price range, seller shop name, and average customer rating.

Authentication is not required for browsing products. Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient navigation through large product catalogs.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_products table with pagination and filtering.

Apply WHERE deleted_at IS NULL to exclude deleted products.
Apply name filter using trigram similarity search (gin_trgm_ops index) for partial matching.
Apply category_id filter when provided.
Apply price range filters (min_price, max_price) against base_price column.
Apply in_stock filter by joining with shopping_mall_product_variants and checking stock_quantity > 0.

Support sorting by:
- created_at DESC (newest)
- base_price ASC (price low-high)
- base_price DESC (price high-low)

Implement cursor-based pagination with limit and cursor parameters.
Return IPageIShoppingMallProduct.ISummary with product summary fields.

Join with shopping_mall_sellers for seller shop name.
Join with shopping_mall_product_images to get first image (index 0) as thumbnail.
Calculate price range if variants have price overrides.
Calculate average rating from shopping_mall_reviews.

Handle edge cases:
- Empty result set: return empty array with null cursor
- Invalid cursor: return error
- No variants: show base_price, mark as unavailable

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summaries with search metadata

requestBody.description: Search criteria including name query, category filter, price range, stock availability, pagination, and sorting options

operations.description:
Retrieve complete details for a specific product by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the full product information including name, description, base price, category assignment, seller details, all product images, and available variants. The response includes comprehensive data needed to render a product detail page with all purchasing options.

Products that have been deleted by the seller (deleted_at is set) will return a 404 Not Found error. This ensures customers cannot access products that are no longer available on the platform.

The product detail includes aggregated rating information calculated from customer reviews, enabling customers to see the average rating and review count before making a purchase decision.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_products table by productId UUID.
Return 404 if product not found or deleted_at is not null.
Join with shopping_mall_sellers to include seller profile information (shop name, logo).
Join with shopping_mall_categories to include category hierarchy.
Include related shopping_mall_product_images ordered by index (first image is thumbnail).
Include related shopping_mall_product_variants with their option values.
Calculate average rating from shopping_mall_reviews for this product.
Return complete IShoppingMallProduct DTO with all nested relations.

responseBody.description: Complete product details including images, variants, seller info, and ratings

operations.description:
Create a new product listing on the shopping mall platform.

This operation allows sellers to create products for sale by providing the product name, description, category assignment, and base price. All four fields are required and the product cannot be created without them. The category can be either a main category or a subcategory.

The product is automatically associated with the authenticated seller who created it and becomes their property. Upon successful creation, the product is immediately visible in search results and category listings.

The system creates an initial product snapshot to preserve the product state at creation time for audit trail purposes.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product record in the shopping_mall_products table.

1. Validate authenticated user is a seller with approved status
2. Validate all required fields: name (non-empty string), description (non-empty string), category_id (valid UUID referencing shopping_mall_categories), base_price (positive number)
3. Verify category_id exists in shopping_mall_categories table
4. Set seller_id from authenticated seller's session
5. Generate UUID for product id
6. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
7. Set deleted_at to null
8. Insert product record into shopping_mall_products table
9. Create initial product snapshot in shopping_mall_product_snapshots table
10. Return the created product entity

Error handling:
- 400: Missing required fields, invalid category_id, non-positive base_price
- 403: User is not an approved seller
- 404: Category not found

responseBody.description: The created product entity with all fields populated

requestBody.description: Product creation data with required fields for listing

operations.description:
Update an existing product's information including name, description, category, and base price.

This operation allows sellers to modify their own product listings. Sellers can update any combination of fields (name, description, category_id, base_price) - partial updates are supported. The category can be either a main category or a subcategory.

The system validates that the product belongs to the requesting seller before allowing updates. Products that have been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null) cannot be updated.

Upon successful update, the product's updated_at timestamp is refreshed and a new snapshot is automatically created in the product snapshots table. This snapshot preserves the complete product state before modification for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes, as required by business rules.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate that the product exists and is not deleted (deleted_at is null). Verify that the requesting seller owns the product by checking seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID. Check for pending order items with paid or shipped status referencing this product - reject if found. Check for pending cancellation or refund requests referencing this product's variants - reject if found. Update the product record with the provided name, description, category_id, and base_price. Set updated_at to current timestamp. Create a new snapshot record in shopping_mall_product_snapshots table capturing the complete product state before modification. Return the updated product entity with all fields including seller and category relationships.

responseBody.description: The updated product entity with all fields

requestBody.description: Product update data with optional fields for partial updates

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before it can be updated - the productId path parameter references an existing product entity

operations.description:
Delete a product from the seller's catalog, removing it from search results and category listings.

This operation soft-deletes the product by setting the deleted_at timestamp. The product becomes invisible to customers and cannot be purchased, but all data is preserved in the system. Product snapshots remain accessible to the seller and administrators for historical records and dispute resolution.

Deletion is subject to business constraints: the product cannot be deleted if any variant has pending order items with paid or shipped status, or if there are any pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant. When deletion succeeds, all associated product variants are automatically cascade-deleted.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a product by productId after validating business constraints.

1. Verify the product exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (check seller_id matches).
2. Check for pending order items: Query shopping_mall_order_items where shopping_mall_product_id = productId AND status IN ('paid', 'shipped'). If any exist, reject with 409 Conflict.
3. Check for pending cancellation requests: Query shopping_mall_cancellation_requests joined with order_items where product matches AND status = 'pending'. If any exist, reject with 409 Conflict.
4. Check for pending refund requests: Query shopping_mall_refund_requests joined with order_items where product matches AND status = 'pending'. If any exist, reject with 409 Conflict.
5. If all validations pass, soft-delete the product by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.
6. Cascade deletion automatically removes all shopping_mall_product_variants (onDelete: Cascade).
7. Return 204 No Content on success.

Error cases:
- 404 Not Found: Product does not exist or already deleted
- 403 Forbidden: Product does not belong to the authenticated seller
- 409 Conflict: Deletion blocked due to pending orders or requests

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before it can be deleted - the productId path parameter must reference an existing product record

operations.description:
Permanently delete a product and all its associated variants from the seller's catalog.

This operation removes the product from search results and category listings. The deletion is subject to business constraints: the product cannot be deleted if any variant has pending order items with paid or shipped status, or if there are any pending cancellation or refund requests for any variant.

When a product is deleted, all associated product variants and their inventory records are automatically deleted through cascade deletion. Product snapshots are preserved for historical order records and remain accessible to the seller and administrators. Deleted products cannot be recovered through the API.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a product by productId after validating business constraints.

1. Verify the product exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (check seller_id matches).
2. Check for pending order items: Query shopping_mall_order_items where shopping_mall_product_id = productId AND status IN ('paid', 'shipped'). If any exist, reject with 409 Conflict.
3. Check for pending cancellation requests: Query shopping_mall_cancellation_requests joined with order_items where product matches AND status = 'pending'. If any exist, reject with 409 Conflict.
4. Check for pending refund requests: Query shopping_mall_refund_requests joined with order_items where product matches AND status = 'pending'. If any exist, reject with 409 Conflict.
5. If all validations pass, soft-delete the product by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.
6. Cascade deletion automatically removes all shopping_mall_product_variants (onDelete: Cascade).
7. Return 204 No Content on success.

Error cases:
- 404 Not Found: Product does not exist or already deleted
- 403 Forbidden: Product does not belong to the authenticated seller
- 409 Conflict: Deletion blocked due to pending orders or requests

prerequisites.description: Category must exist before a product can be created with a valid category_id foreign key reference
Product must be created before it can be deleted by the administrator

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product variants for a specific product.

This operation provides sellers with the ability to browse and search through variants of their product. Supports filtering by SKU code, price range, and creation date. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

Variants are returned with their current configuration including SKU code, price override, and option combinations. Only the product owner (seller) can access variants for their products.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_product_variants table filtered by shopping_mall_product_id. Apply search filters from request body: sku_code partial match, price_override range, created_at range. Join with shopping_mall_product_variant_options and shopping_mall_product_option_values to include option combinations in response. Apply pagination with cursor or offset-based approach. Sort by specified field (created_at, sku_code, price_override) in specified direction. Verify product ownership - seller can only access their own product's variants. Return 404 if product not found or user lacks permission. Return empty array if no variants match criteria.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product variant summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering variants

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before variants can be listed, as variants have a foreign key dependency on the parent product

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific product variant.

This operation returns complete variant details including SKU code, price override, and selected option values. The variant is accessed through its parent product to ensure proper ownership validation.

Returns the full variant entity with all associated option values representing the specific configuration (e.g., Color=Red, Size=Large). Includes timestamps for creation and last modification.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_product_variants table by variant ID.
Validate that the variant belongs to the specified product by checking shopping_mall_product_id matches productId parameter.
Join with shopping_mall_product_variant_options to retrieve selected option values.
Join with shopping_mall_product_option_values to get option value names.
Return 404 if variant not found or doesn't belong to the specified product.
Exclude soft-deleted variants (deleted_at is not null).

responseBody.description: Complete product variant details with option values

operations.description:
Create a new product variant (SKU) for an existing product.

This operation allows sellers to add variants to their products. Each variant represents a specific combination of option values (such as Color=Red, Size=Large) with a unique SKU code. Variants can have an optional price override that supersedes the parent product's base price.

The variant is created with an initial stock quantity of zero. Sellers must subsequently add inventory through the inventory management endpoints. A product must have at least one variant to be purchasable by customers.

The SKU code must be globally unique across all variants in the system. Option values must belong to option definitions of the parent product.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the authenticated user is the seller who owns the product. Verify product exists and is not deleted. Validate SKU code is globally unique (check shopping_mall_product_variants.sku_code uniqueness constraint). Validate all provided option value IDs belong to option definitions of this product. Create the variant record with shopping_mall_product_id, sku_code, price_override (nullable), and timestamps. Create junction records in shopping_mall_product_variant_options linking the variant to each selected option value. Return the created variant with its option values joined. Handle uniqueness violation on SKU code with 409 Conflict. Handle invalid option value ownership with 400 Bad Request.

responseBody.description: The created product variant with its option value combinations

parameters.description: Product ID (UUID format) - the parent product to add the variant to
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Variant creation data including SKU code, optional price override, and option value IDs

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before variants can be added to it, as variant creation requires a valid productId referencing an existing product
Option definitions must exist to define configurable attribute types (e.g., Color, Size) that option values will belong to
Option values must be created before they can be referenced in the option_value_ids array when creating a variant

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant's configuration including SKU code, price override, and option value combinations.

This operation allows sellers to modify their product variants. The variant must belong to a product owned by the requesting seller. Updating a variant creates an immutable snapshot preserving the previous state for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

The SKU code must be unique across all variants in the system. Option values define the variant's specific configuration such as color, size, or material combinations. Price override is optional - when null, the parent product's base price applies.

The system validates that the variant exists, is not soft-deleted, the seller owns the parent product, and the new SKU code is not already in use. Pending order items do not block variant updates (unlike deletions per section 322), but the updated information applies to future orders only.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting seller owns the product by checking shopping_mall_products.seller_id matches authenticated seller.

Validate variant exists in shopping_mall_product_variants with matching id and shopping_mall_product_id.

Check SKU code uniqueness: query shopping_mall_product_variants.sku_code to ensure no duplicate (excluding current variant).

Begin database transaction:
1. Update shopping_mall_product_variants record with new sku_code, price_override, and updated_at timestamp.
2. Delete existing shopping_mall_product_variant_options records for this variant.
3. Insert new shopping_mall_product_variant_options records linking variant to provided option_value_ids.
4. Create snapshot record in shopping_mall_product_variant_snapshots capturing all fields before update.
5. Commit transaction.

Return updated variant entity with joined option values.

Error handling:
- 404: Product or variant not found
- 403: Seller does not own the product
- 409: SKU code already exists
- 400: Invalid option value IDs or empty option values array

responseBody.description: Updated product variant entity with complete information

parameters.description: Parent product ID (UUID format, used for ownership verification)
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Variant update data including SKU code, optional price override, and option value IDs

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before variants can be added or updated, as variants belong to a parent product via foreign key relationship
Option values must exist before being referenced in a variant's option_value_ids array, as the update operation validates all option value IDs belong to the parent product's option definitions
Variant must be created before it can be updated, as the update operation validates the variant exists and is not soft-deleted

operations.description:
Permanently remove a product variant from the catalog.

This operation deletes a specific variant (SKU) from a product. The variant must have no pending order items in paid or shipped status, no pending cancellation requests, and no pending refund requests. Additionally, the product must have at least one other variant remaining after deletion to remain purchasable.

When a variant is deleted, all inventory records for that variant are also removed. The variant no longer appears in product listings or search results. This operation is performed by the seller who owns the product.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting user is the seller who owns the product. Verify the variant exists and belongs to the specified product.

Check deletion preconditions:
1. Query order_items table for any items referencing this variant with status 'paid' or 'shipped' - reject if found
2. Query cancellation_requests table for any pending requests for this variant - reject if found
3. Query refund_requests table for any pending requests for this variant - reject if found
4. Count remaining variants for this product - reject if this is the last variant (product would have zero variants)

If all validations pass, set deleted_at timestamp on the variant record. Cascade delete all inventory_records for this variant. Return 204 No Content on success.

Handle edge cases: concurrent deletion attempts should use optimistic locking. If product itself is deleted, variants are cascade deleted automatically.

parameters.description: Variant ID (UUID format, scoped to product)
parameters.name: variantId

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before variants can be added to it
Variant must be created before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product option definitions for a specific product.

This operation returns all option type definitions (such as Color, Size, Material) associated with the specified product. Each option definition represents a configurable attribute type that customers can select when choosing a product variant.

Supports pagination for products with many option types. Option definitions are managed by the product's seller and are used to define the available variant combinations. Deleted option definitions are excluded from results.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_product_option_definitions table filtered by shopping_mall_product_id matching the path parameter.
Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL).
Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based strategy.
Support optional filtering by option definition name (partial match).
Join with shopping_mall_product_option_values if option values need to be included in response.
Return paginated list with option definition summaries including id, name, and creation timestamp.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product option definition summaries

parameters.description: Product ID (UUID format) - the parent product whose option definitions to retrieve
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering option definitions

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific product option definition by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a single option definition (such as Color, Size, or Material) that belongs to a specific product. Option definitions define the configurable attributes that customers can select when purchasing a product variant.

The endpoint validates that the option definition belongs to the specified product before returning the data. If the product or option definition does not exist, or if the option definition belongs to a different product, the request returns a 404 Not Found response.

This operation is typically used by sellers managing their product configurations or by customers viewing available option types when selecting product variants.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_product_option_definitions table by primary key (id = optionDefinitionId).

Validate that the retrieved option definition's shopping_mall_product_id matches the provided productId parameter. If no match or record not found, return 404.

Check deleted_at field - if the option definition is soft-deleted, return 404 to hide it from consumers.

Return the complete option definition record including id, shopping_mall_product_id, name, created_at, and updated_at fields.

No joins required as this is a single-table lookup. Ensure proper indexing on id column for fast retrieval.

responseBody.description: Complete product option definition details

parameters.description: Product option definition ID (UUID format, global scope)
parameters.name: optionDefinitionId

operations.description:
Create a new product option definition for a specific product.

This operation allows sellers to add configurable option types to their products, such as 'Color', 'Size', or 'Material'. Each option definition serves as a container for multiple option values that customers can select when purchasing the product.

The option definition name must be unique within the product. Attempting to create a duplicate option type name for the same product will result in a conflict error. Once created, option definitions can have values added to them through separate operations.

Only the seller who owns the product can add option definitions to it. The operation validates product ownership before creation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that the productId exists and belongs to the authenticated seller. Check that no option definition with the same name already exists for this product (enforce composite unique constraint on shopping_mall_product_id and name). Create the shopping_mall_product_option_definitions record with the provided name, linking it to the product. Set created_at and updated_at timestamps to current time. Return the complete created option definition entity including the generated UUID.

responseBody.description: The newly created product option definition

requestBody.description: Option definition creation data

operations.description:
Update an existing product option definition such as Color, Size, or Material.

This operation allows sellers to modify the name of an option definition in the shopping_mall_product_option_definitions table. Option definitions represent configurable attribute types that customers can select when purchasing a product, such as 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', or 'Style'. Each option definition belongs to a specific product and has multiple available values stored in shopping_mall_product_option_values.

The option definition name must be unique within the product due to the composite unique constraint on (shopping_mall_product_id, name). Attempting to update to a name that already exists for the same product will be rejected. This operation is restricted to the seller who owns the parent product.

All option values associated with this definition remain unchanged. The update only affects the option definition's display name and updates the updated_at timestamp. Soft-deleted option definitions (where deleted_at is not null) cannot be updated.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate that the product exists and is owned by the authenticated seller. Verify the option definition exists and belongs to the specified product. Check that the new name is not empty and does not duplicate an existing option definition name for the same product. Update the option definition name and updated_at timestamp. Return the complete updated option definition entity. If product or option definition not found, return 404. If name conflict exists, return 400 validation error. If seller does not own the product, return 403 forbidden.

responseBody.description: The updated product option definition with all fields including id, shopping_mall_product_id, name, created_at, updated_at

operations.description:
Delete a product option definition and all its associated option values.

This operation soft-deletes an option definition (such as Color, Size, or Material) from a product by setting the deleted_at timestamp. All option values belonging to this definition (e.g., Red, Blue, Large, Small) are also soft-deleted through cascade deletion.

Only the seller who owns the product can delete its option definitions. The operation verifies that the product belongs to the requesting seller before proceeding. Deleted option definitions are hidden from product configuration interfaces but remain preserved in product snapshots for historical reference.

This action can be reversed by restoring the deleted_at timestamp. However, if the option definition is referenced by existing product variants, those variants will retain their option value associations in snapshots.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete shopping_mall_product_option_definitions record by ID with product ownership verification.

1. Verify the product exists and belongs to the requesting seller
2. Verify the option definition exists and belongs to the specified product
3. Delete the option definition record (sets deleted_at timestamp)
4. Cascade deletion automatically removes all associated shopping_mall_product_variant_options records
5. Cascade deletion automatically removes all associated shopping_mall_product_option_values records
6. Return 204 No Content on success
7. Return 404 if product or option definition not found
8. Return 403 if seller does not own the product

Edge cases:
- Option definition referenced by existing variants: variants remain but lose option value associations
- Concurrent deletion: handle with optimistic locking on updated_at timestamp

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product option values for a specific option definition.

This operation returns all available values (e.g., Red, Blue, Large, Small) for a given product option definition (e.g., Color, Size). Option values are used to construct product variant combinations and are managed by sellers through their product management workflows.

Supports pagination for option definitions with many values. Results are scoped to the specified option definition and product, ensuring data isolation and access control.

Query shopping_mall_product_option_values table filtered by shopping_mall_product_option_definition_id.

Apply pagination parameters (page, limit) and optional search filters on option value name.

Join with shopping_mall_product_option_definitions to verify product ownership and access control.

Return cursor-based or offset pagination with option value summaries including id, name, and timestamps.

Retrieve a specific product option value within its option definition and product context.

This operation returns the complete details of a product option value, including its display name and metadata. Option values represent the available choices for a product option type, such as 'Red' or 'Blue' for a Color option, or 'Large' or 'Small' for a Size option.

The nested path structure reflects the hierarchical relationship: option values belong to option definitions, which belong to products. This endpoint is useful for displaying option selection interfaces in product customization flows or validating option value existence before variant creation.

Returns the option value entity with id, name, created_at, and updated_at fields. Only active (non-deleted) option values are accessible through this endpoint.

Return the option value entity with id, name, created_at, and updated_at fields.

Create a new option value under a specific product option definition.

This operation allows sellers to add available values (such as 'Red', 'Blue', 'Large', 'Small') to an existing option definition (such as 'Color' or 'Size') for their product. Option values are used to construct product variant combinations that customers can select when purchasing.

The option value name must be unique within its parent option definition. Attempting to create a duplicate value name under the same option definition will be rejected. Option values are managed exclusively through their parent product and are automatically deleted when the product is deleted.

This operation is restricted to the seller who owns the product. Administrators can also perform this operation for any product on the platform.

Validate that the optionDefinitionId exists and belongs to the specified product. operations.description:

This operation allows sellers to delete specific option values (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Small') from their product's option definitions. The option value is marked as deleted and will no longer appear in product configuration interfaces or be available for creating new product variants.

The system enforces strict validation before deletion: the option value must not be currently referenced by any active (non-deleted) product variants. If any variant uses this option value, the deletion request is rejected with a conflict error to maintain data integrity and prevent orphaned references.

Only the product owner (seller) can delete option values from their products. Deleted option values are preserved in the database with a deletion timestamp and remain visible in historical snapshots for audit and dispute resolution purposes. This operation does not affect existing variants that were created before the deletion.

If any active variants exist, reject the deletion with an error indicating the option value is in use.

Perform soft delete by setting shopping_mall_product_option_values.deleted_at to the current timestamp.

Return 204 No Content on success. Return 404 if any of the resources (product, option definition, or option value) are not found or already deleted. Return 403 if the seller does not own the product. Return 409 if the option value is currently used in active variants.

operations.description:
Adjust inventory stock quantity for a specific product variant by creating a new inventory record.

This operation allows sellers to manage stock levels for their product variants by recording inventory changes. Positive quantity_change values represent restocking (adding inventory), while negative values represent stock reductions due to adjustments, losses, or manual corrections.

Each inventory adjustment requires a reason explaining the change, such as restock, damaged goods, inventory correction, or promotional allocation. The system maintains an immutable audit trail of all stock movements, and the current stock quantity is calculated by summing all quantity_change values for the variant.

The variant must belong to a product owned by the authenticated seller. The operation validates that the variant exists and is not deleted. After successful adjustment, the new inventory record is returned with the calculated current stock level.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the product exists and is owned by the authenticated seller.
Validate that the variant exists, belongs to the specified product, and is not deleted.
Validate quantity_change is non-zero (must be positive for restock or negative for adjustment).
Validate reason is provided and not empty.
Create a new shopping_mall_product_inventory_records entry with product_variant_id, quantity_change, reason, and created_at timestamp.
Calculate current stock by summing all quantity_change values for this variant from shopping_mall_product_inventory_records.
Return the created inventory record with current stock quantity.
Handle edge cases: variant not found, variant belongs to different product, seller doesn't own product, zero quantity_change, empty reason.

responseBody.description: Created inventory record with current stock quantity

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific inventory record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single stock movement event, including the quantity change amount, reason code, and timestamp. Inventory records are immutable audit trail entries that track all stock changes for product variants.

Records are automatically created during order placement, cancellation, refund processing, and manual seller inventory adjustments. This endpoint provides access to individual records for audit and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: at

Query shopping_mall_inventory_records table by record ID.

Verify the inventory record exists and the associated variant belongs to the specified product:

2. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to get product_variant_id
3. Verify shopping_mall_product_id matches productId
4. Return 404 if record not found or product/variant mismatch

Return complete inventory record with all fields: id, product_variant_id, quantity_change, reason, created_at.

Authorization: Only seller who owns the product can access inventory records for their variants.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of inventory records for stock quantity change tracking.

This operation provides comprehensive inventory history viewing capabilities including filtering by product variant, reason code, and date ranges. Records are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order (newest first) to show recent stock movements prominently.

Inventory records are immutable audit trail entries that capture every stock quantity change. Each record shows the quantity change amount (positive for restocking, negative for orders/adjustments), reason code, and timestamp. Current stock quantity is calculated by summing all quantity_change values for a variant.

This endpoint supports sellers monitoring their inventory movements and administrators auditing stock changes across the platform. Records are automatically created during order placement, cancellation, refund processing, and manual inventory adjustments.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single inventory record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete details of a specific inventory change event, including the quantity change amount, reason code, and timestamp. Inventory records form an immutable audit trail of all stock movements for product variants.

Only sellers can access inventory records, and only for product variants they own. The operation enforces ownership validation through the product variant relationship. Records cannot be modified or deleted once created, ensuring a permanent historical record of all inventory changes.

The response includes the product variant reference, enabling sellers to understand which variant's stock was affected by this change event.

operations.description:
Create a manual inventory adjustment record for a product variant.

This operation allows sellers to manually adjust inventory levels for their product variants. Positive quantity_change values represent restocking (adding inventory), while negative values represent adjustments for losses, damages, or corrections.

Each inventory record must include a reason explaining the adjustment. Records are immutable once created and cannot be modified or deleted.

This endpoint is for manual adjustments only. Automatic inventory records are created by the system during order placement, cancellations, and refunds. The seller must own the product variant being adjusted, validated through the product variant's parent product relationship.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new inventory record for manual seller adjustment.

1. Validate seller authentication and extract seller_id from session
2. Load product_variant by product_variant_id
3. Traverse product_variant → product to verify seller_id matches authenticated seller
4. Validate quantity_change is non-zero integer
5. Validate reason is non-empty string
6. Create inventory_record with: id (UUID), product_variant_id, quantity_change, reason, created_at (current timestamp)
7. Return created record

Business rules:
- Records are immutable (no update/delete operations)
- quantity_change: positive for restock, negative for adjustment/loss
- reason is required and cannot be empty
- Seller must own the variant (via product ownership)
- Automatic records from orders/cancellations/refunds use system endpoints, not this manual adjustment endpoint

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of products in the authenticated customer's wishlist.

This operation returns all products the customer has saved to their wishlist, including product details such as main image, name, price or price range, seller shop name, and current availability status. The wishlist displays products at the product level rather than specific variants.

Supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by addition date (newest or oldest first). Each wishlist item shows whether the product is still available for purchase or has been deleted/unavailable. Products automatically removed from wishlists when deleted by sellers are not included in results.

Only the authenticated customer can access their own wishlist. The operation filters results to show only products that are currently available on the platform.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_wishlist_items table filtered by authenticated customer's ID.

Join with shopping_mall_products to retrieve product information including name, description, base price, and main image (first product image).
Join with shopping_mall_sellers through product to get seller shop name.
Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to calculate price range if multiple variants exist.
Check variant stock quantities to determine availability status.

Apply pagination using cursor-based or offset pagination on created_at field.
Support sorting by created_at ascending or descending.

Filter out wishlist items where product has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null).
Filter out products where all variants are out of stock if in-stock-only filter is applied.

Return IPageIShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary with wishlist items containing product summary information and availability indicators.

Handle edge cases:
- Empty wishlist: return empty page with zero items
- All products unavailable: return empty results or items marked unavailable based on requirement
- Invalid pagination parameters: use defaults

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific wishlist item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single product saved in the customer's wishlist, including the product details such as name, description, main image, base price or price range, seller information, and average rating.

The wishlist item is scoped to the authenticated customer's account. Customers can only access wishlist items that belong to their own wishlist. If the product has been deleted by the seller or is no longer available, the wishlist item will not be found.

This endpoint is useful for displaying detailed product information when a customer clicks on a specific item from their wishlist view.
operations.name: at

Query shopping_mall_wishlist_items table by the provided wishlistItemId UUID.

Verify that the wishlist item belongs to the authenticated customer by checking customer_id matches the session user.

Join with shopping_mall_products to retrieve complete product information including name, description, category, and seller details.

Include product's main image (first image from shopping_mall_product_images where product_id matches).

Calculate price range if product has multiple variants with different prices.

Include average rating from shopping_mall_reviews if reviews exist for the product.

operations.description:
Add a product to the authenticated customer's personal wishlist.

This operation creates a new wishlist entry linking the customer to a product they are interested in for future purchase consideration. The wishlist stores products at the product level, not specific variants, allowing customers to track entire products rather than particular option combinations.

The system enforces duplicate prevention - if the product already exists in the customer's wishlist, the request is rejected. The product must exist and not be deleted by the seller. The customer must be authenticated to access this feature.

Upon successful addition, the wishlist entry is created with a timestamp for sorting and pagination purposes. The created entry includes the product reference and creation timestamp.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new wishlist item for the authenticated customer.

1. Extract customer_id from authenticated session token
2. Validate product_id exists in shopping_mall_products table
3. Check product.deleted_at is null (product not deleted)
4. Check for existing wishlist entry: query shopping_mall_wishlist_items where customer_id and product_id match
5. If duplicate exists, return 409 Conflict error
6. If product deleted or not found, return 404 Not Found error
7. Insert new record into shopping_mall_wishlist_items with customer_id, product_id, created_at, updated_at
8. Return created wishlist item with full entity data

Edge cases:
- Product deleted by seller: reject with 404
- Duplicate wishlist entry: reject with 409
- Unauthenticated request: reject with 401
- Invalid product_id format: reject with 400

responseBody.description: Created wishlist item with product reference and timestamps

requestBody.description: Product identifier to add to wishlist. Only product_id is required; customer_id is automatically derived from the authenticated session.

operations.description:
Remove a specific product from the customer's wishlist.

This operation permanently deletes a wishlist item entry, removing the association between the customer and the saved product. The deletion is immediate and cannot be undone.

Only the customer who owns the wishlist can remove items from it. If the wishlist item does not exist or has already been removed (including automatic cleanup when a product is deleted), the request is rejected. The removal of a product from the wishlist does not affect the product itself or other customers' wishlists.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the wishlist item record by UUID from shopping_mall_wishlist_items table.

Validate that the wishlist item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer. Check that the item is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at timestamp to current time.

Return 404 if the wishlist item does not exist or does not belong to the customer. Return 404 if the item was already deleted (including automatic cleanup from product deletion). No response body on successful deletion.

prerequisites.description: Wishlist item must be created before it can be deleted - the delete operation requires an existing wishlist item record to remove

Join with shopping_mall_cart_items for item count aggregation and total price calculation. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_products for product information in cart items. Join with shopping_mall_customers for customer information if requested.
