operations.description:
Retrieve a specific shopping cart by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete cart entity including all cart items with their product variant details, quantities, prices, and subtotals. The cart belongs to a specific customer and persists across sessions, serving as a staging area for items intended for purchase.

The response includes the cart's metadata (creation date, last update) and an array of cart items. Each item contains the product variant reference, quantity, unit price snapshot, and calculated subtotal. Items marked as unavailable (deleted variants or out of stock) are indicated in the response.

Customers can only access their own carts. Attempting to access another customer's cart will result in an authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_carts table by primary key ID.

Include eager loading of cart items via the items relation, joining with shopping_mall_product_variants to get variant details.

Filter to exclude soft-deleted items (deleted_at IS NULL) from the items array.

Verify the cart's customer_id matches the authenticated user's ID for authorization.

Return 404 if cart not found or does not belong to the authenticated customer.

Calculate subtotal for each item (price × quantity) and total cart value in the service layer if not denormalized in the response type.

responseBody.description: Complete cart entity with all items and calculated totals

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a cart item or remove it from the shopping cart.

This operation allows customers to modify the quantity of an existing cart item. The quantity can be increased or decreased, but must remain at least 1. Setting the quantity to 0 or using the remove flag will delete the item from the cart. The cart total is automatically recalculated after the update.

Cart items are marked as unavailable if the product variant has been deleted by the seller or is out of stock. Unavailable items cannot be updated and will return an error. The operation validates that the cart item belongs to the authenticated customer.
operations.name: putByCartitemid
operations.specification: Update shopping_mall_cart_items record by cartItemId. Validate that the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer's cart (join with shopping_mall_carts on customer_id). Check that the item is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). If quantity is provided and >= 1, update the quantity field and set updated_at. If quantity is 0 or remove flag is true, perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp. Validate that the product variant still exists and is purchasable. Return 404 if cart item not found. Return 400 if quantity < 0. Return 400 if item is unavailable (variant deleted or out of stock). Return updated cart item on success.

responseBody.description: Updated cart item with new quantity or soft delete confirmation

requestBody.description: Cart item update request with quantity or removal flag

prerequisites.description: Cart item must be created before it can be updated - the cartItemId path parameter references an existing cart item that was added via the create operation

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific shopping cart item by its unique identifier within the customer's cart.

This operation returns the complete details of a single active cart item, including the product variant reference, quantity, unit price snapshot, and temporal metadata. The price field represents the unit price captured at the time the item was added to the cart, ensuring consistent display and checkout calculation even if the product variant's price changes later.

Cart items are subsidiary entities belonging to a customer's shopping cart. Each item references a specific product variant and maintains a unique constraint on (cart_id, product_variant_id) to prevent duplicate variants within the same cart. Only active (non-deleted) items are returned through this endpoint.

The cart item includes soft delete support via the deleted_at field. Items with a non-null deleted_at value are considered removed from the cart and are excluded from this operation's results. This ensures customers only see active items in their cart.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shopping_mall_cart_items table by the provided item UUID.

1. Validate the itemId is a valid UUID format
2. Query shopping_mall_cart_items WHERE id = itemId
3. Include soft-deleted items in the result (do not filter by deleted_at)
4. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants if variant details are needed in response
5. Join with shopping_mall_carts to verify cart ownership if authorization is required
6. Return 404 if no cart item exists with the given ID
7. Return the full IShoppingMallCartItem entity with all fields

Authorization: Verify the requesting customer owns the cart containing this item (via cart.customer_id match with authenticated user).

Edge cases:
- Item not found: return 404
- Item belongs to different customer: return 404 or 403 based on authorization policy
- Soft-deleted item: still return the entity (deleted_at will be populated)

responseBody.description: Complete cart item entity with all fields for active items only

operations.description:
Add a product variant to the customer's shopping cart.

This operation adds a specified product variant to the authenticated customer's cart with the requested quantity. If the same variant already exists in the cart, the quantities are combined rather than creating a duplicate entry. The unit price is captured as a snapshot from the product variant at the time of addition, ensuring consistent pricing even if the variant's price changes later.

The cart persists across sessions, so items remain in the cart until the customer removes them or completes a purchase. After successful order placement, items included in the order are automatically removed from the cart.

Requests are rejected if the product variant does not exist, has been deleted by the seller, or is out of stock. The quantity must be at least 1. The response includes the created or updated cart item with the captured price snapshot and current quantity.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the authenticated customer's active cart from shopping_mall_carts using customer_id (from session token).
2. If no cart exists, create a new cart record for the customer.
3. Query shopping_mall_product_variants to verify the variant exists and is active (deleted_at is null).
4. Check if a cart item already exists for this (cart_id, product_variant_id) pair.
5. If exists: update the quantity by adding the new quantity to existing quantity, update updated_at.
6. If not exists: create new cart item with price snapshot from variant.price_override (or parent product base price if override is null).
7. Set created_at for new items, updated_at for all operations.
8. Return the cart item entity with all fields including the captured price.
9. Handle edge cases: variant not found (404), variant deleted (400), invalid quantity <= 0 (400).

responseBody.description: The created or updated cart item with captured price snapshot

requestBody.description: Product variant identifier and quantity to add to cart

operations.description:
Update the quantity of a specific item in the customer's shopping cart.

This operation allows customers to modify the quantity of an existing cart item. When the quantity is updated, the cart total price is recalculated to reflect the change. Customers can adjust quantities at any time before proceeding to checkout.

Setting the quantity to zero removes the item from the cart entirely. The item must belong to the authenticated customer's cart. Attempting to update an item from another customer's cart will result in an authorization error. If the item does not exist or has been removed, a not found error is returned.
operations.name: putByItemid
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_cart_items table by itemId.
Verify the cart item belongs to the authenticated customer by joining with shopping_mall_carts on cart_id.
Validate quantity is a positive integer (minimum 1).
Update the quantity field and set updated_at to current timestamp.
Return the updated cart item with all fields including price snapshot.
Handle edge cases: item not found (404), item belongs to different customer (403), invalid quantity (400).

responseBody.description: The updated cart item with new quantity and deletion status

requestBody.description: Updated quantity for the cart item. Set to 0 to remove the item from cart.

prerequisites.description: Product must exist before variants can be created and added to cart
Product variant must exist before it can be added to a shopping cart
Cart item must be created before it can be updated with new quantity

operations.description:
Remove a specific item from the customer's shopping cart.

This operation allows customers to delete individual cart items by their unique identifier. When an item is removed, it is soft-deleted from the cart and the cart total is recalculated. The removal affects only the specified item, leaving all other cart items unchanged.

Removing a cart item does not affect the customer's wishlist - products saved to the wishlist remain intact. If the item was unavailable (out of stock or deleted product), it can still be removed from the cart using this endpoint.

The operation implements soft-delete behavior, marking the item with a deleted_at timestamp rather than permanently removing it from the database for audit trail purposes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the cart item with the given itemId from the shopping_mall_cart_items table.

1. Verify the cart item exists and belongs to the authenticated customer's cart by joining with shopping_mall_carts on shopping_mall_cart_id
2. Check that deleted_at is null (item not already removed)
3. Soft-delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
4. Recalculate cart total by summing (price * quantity) for all non-deleted items in the cart
5. Return success with no response body

Edge cases:
- Item already deleted: return 404 Not Found
- Item belongs to different customer's cart: return 404 Not Found (do not reveal existence)
- Cart itself is deleted: return 404 Not Found

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before variants can be added and items can be placed in cart
Product variant must exist before it can be added to a customer's shopping cart
Cart item must be created before it can be deleted from the shopping cart

operations.description:
Update quantities or remove items in a customer's shopping cart.

This operation allows customers to modify existing cart items by changing quantities or removing items entirely. Multiple items can be updated in a single request for efficient cart management. When quantity is set to 0 or the remove flag is true, the item is soft deleted from the cart.

The cart total price is recalculated based on the updated quantities. Items marked as unavailable (due to out of stock variants or deleted products) cannot be modified and will be ignored in the update operation.

Only the cart owner (authenticated customer) can modify their cart items. Attempts to modify another customer's cart will be rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate that the cartId exists and belongs to the authenticated customer. For each item update in the request body: verify the cart item exists and is not soft deleted, check that the item is not marked as unavailable. If quantity is provided and greater than 0, update the quantity field. If quantity is 0 or remove flag is true, set deleted_at timestamp to current time. Validate that quantity does not exceed available stock for the variant. After all updates, recalculate cart totals. Return the updated cart items with their current state including availability status.

responseBody.description: Updated cart items with their current state

requestBody.description: Cart item updates with quantity changes or removal flags

prerequisites.description: Cart items must be created before they can be updated; this operation adds product variants to the cart which creates the cart item records that will later be modified

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific item from a customer's shopping cart by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a single cart item including the product variant reference, quantity, unit price snapshot captured at time of addition, and timestamps. The cart item is accessed through its parent cart to ensure proper data isolation and ownership validation.

The unit price is denormalized as a snapshot to maintain consistent display and checkout calculation even if the product variant's price changes after the item was added to the cart. This operation verifies that the cart item belongs to the specified cart and has not been soft deleted.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_cart_items table by item ID with cart ID verification.

1. Verify cart exists and belongs to authenticated customer (data isolation)
2. Verify cart item exists with matching cart_id and item id
3. Verify cart item is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null)
4. Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to include variant details
5. Join with shopping_mall_products for product name and image information
6. Return full cart item entity with variant and product details

Edge cases:
- Cart not found → 404
- Cart item not found → 404
- Cart item belongs to different cart → 404
- Cart item is soft deleted → 404
- Customer does not own the cart → 403

responseBody.description: Complete cart item details including quantity, price snapshot, and product variant information

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated customer's order history.

This operation returns all orders placed by the authenticated customer, sorted by newest orders first. Each order in the list displays the order number, order date, total price, and overall order status. The order status is derived from the aggregate status of all order items within the order (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded).

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and filtering options including order number search, status filtering, and date range queries. Response includes order summary information optimized for list displays, enabling customers to quickly identify recent purchases and track their order statuses. Select any order from the list to view full details including items, shipping address, and shipment information.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_orders table with pagination and filtering.

For customer actor: Filter by customer_id = authenticated user's ID. For administrator actor: no customer filter (return all orders).

Apply search filters on order_number (partial match), status (exact match or array), ordered_at date range (from/to).

Sort by ordered_at DESC by default (newest first). Support custom sorting by order_number, total amount if requested.

Implement cursor-based or offset pagination with limit and page parameters.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to calculate total price if not stored. Include order item count in summary.

Return IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary with pagination metadata (page, limit, total count).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries with pagination metadata including total count, current page, and page size

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering customer orders

operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific order by its ID.

This operation returns the full order information including the order number, order date, total price, overall status, complete shipping address snapshot (as it was at purchase time), all order items with their individual statuses, and associated shipment tracking information.

Customers can only access their own orders. The shipping address is an immutable snapshot preserved from the time of purchase, ensuring order records remain accurate even if the customer later modifies or deletes addresses from their address book.

Order items include product name, variant details, quantity, unit price, and individual item status. Shipments provide tracking carrier, tracking number, and delivery confirmation status.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_orders table by order ID with customer ownership validation.

Verify the authenticated customer owns this order by matching customer_id. Return 404 if order not found or belongs to different customer.

Eager load related order items from shopping_mall_order_items filtered by shopping_mall_order_id. For each order item, include its snapshot from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots containing product_name, variant_sku_code, variant_price, seller_shop_name.

Load associated shipments by joining shopping_mall_shipment_items to shopping_mall_shipments. Include tracking_carrier, tracking_number, shipped_at, confirmed_at for each shipment.

Return complete order with nested orderItems array and shipments array. Handle case where order has no shipments yet (items not shipped).

responseBody.description: Complete order details with items and shipments

operations.description:
Create a new customer order by processing checkout with selected cart items and shipping address.

This operation initiates the order placement workflow by creating a record in the shopping_mall_orders table, capturing the complete transaction state including product variants, quantities, prices, and shipping address snapshot. The shipping address fields (recipient_name, recipient_phone, street_address, city, state, postal_code, country) are stored as immutable snapshots in the order record and cannot be modified after creation, ensuring historical accuracy per requirement [101].

Upon successful order creation, all items from the customer's cart that were included in the order are automatically removed from shopping_mall_cart_items. The order receives a unique order_number for customer-facing reference and support lookup. Order status is derived from the individual order items' statuses in shopping_mall_order_items.

This operation also triggers automatic inventory updates (requirement [75]), creating negative inventory records to deduct stock for each purchased variant.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create order transaction with the following steps:

1. Validate customer has at least one address (required for checkout)
2. Validate all cart items exist and are available (not deleted, sufficient stock)
3. Generate unique order_number (format: ORD-YYYYMMDD-XXXXX)
4. Create shopping_mall_orders record with:
   - customer_id from authenticated session
   - order_number (generated)
   - ordered_at (current timestamp)
   - Shipping address fields snapshotted from selected address (recipient_name, recipient_phone, street_address, city, state, postal_code, country)
5. Create shopping_mall_order_items for each cart item:
   - Link to order, product, product_variant, seller
   - Copy quantity and price from cart item
   - Set initial status to 'paid'
6. Remove ordered items from customer's cart (post-order cleanup)
7. Create inventory records for each variant (stock reduction)
8. Return complete order with all order items

Error handling:
- 400 if customer has no addresses
- 400 if cart is empty
- 400 if any cart item is unavailable (deleted variant, insufficient stock)
- 400 if cart item quantity exceeds available stock
- 409 if order_number generation collision (retry with new number)

responseBody.description: Complete order details from shopping_mall_orders including order number, timestamp, immutable shipping address snapshot, and all order items with product and variant information from shopping_mall_order_items.

requestBody.description: Order creation request containing the selected shipping address ID from shopping_mall_addresses and optional list of cart item IDs to include in the order. If cart items are not specified, all active cart items from shopping_mall_cart_items are included.

prerequisites.description: Customer must have at least one shipping address before placing an order, as the order creation requires a valid shopping_mall_address_id to snapshot address fields for immutable order record
Customer must have items in their shopping cart before creating an order, as order creation processes cart items and fails with 400 error if cart is empty

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items within a specific order.

This operation provides detailed access to individual items within an order, supporting status-based filtering to identify items at different fulfillment stages. Each order item represents a purchased product variant with its quantity, price, and current status tracked independently.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Response includes order item summary information with product details, variant options, and seller information optimized for list displays. Useful for order detail views, seller fulfillment dashboards, and administrative order management.

Authorization requirements vary by actor: customers can only access items from their own orders, sellers can access items containing their products, and administrators have full access to all order items.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_order_items table filtered by shopping_mall_order_id. Apply status filters if provided in request body (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded). Support pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach. Join with shopping_mall_products for product name, shopping_mall_product_variants for variant options, and shopping_mall_sellers for seller information. Return order item summaries optimized for list display. Validate that orderId exists in shopping_mall_orders table. Apply authorization: customers can only access their own orders, sellers can access items from their products, administrators can access all orders. Handle edge case where order has no items (return empty page). Sort by created_at descending by default, allow override via request body.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries

parameters.description: Order ID (UUID format, scoped to specific order)
parameters.name: orderId

requestBody.description: Search criteria including status filters, pagination, and sorting parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within an order.

This operation returns complete details of an individual order item including the purchased product, variant, quantity, unit price, and current item status. The order item represents one SKU purchased by a customer as part of a larger order.

Customers can access order items from their own orders only. The response includes all item metadata necessary for displaying order details, tracking item status through the fulfillment lifecycle, and supporting cancellation or refund workflows.

The order item status indicates the current fulfillment state: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded. Each item in an order can have an independent status, enabling partial shipment and individual item cancellation scenarios.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_items table by primary key ID.

Validate that the order item exists and belongs to the specified order by checking shopping_mall_order_id matches the orderId parameter.

Verify customer authorization: ensure the parent order's customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID.

Join with shopping_mall_products to include product name and details.
Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to include variant option information.
Join with shopping_mall_sellers to include seller shop information.

Return the complete order item record with all fields: id, quantity, price, status, created_at, updated_at.

Handle edge cases:
- Order item not found: return 404
- Order item belongs to different order: return 404
- Customer not authorized to view this order: return 403
- Soft-deleted order item: return 404

responseBody.description: Complete order item details including product, variant, and seller information

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before its items can be retrieved. Order items are generated as part of the order placement process.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items.

This operation provides flexible querying of order items with support for filtering by order, seller, status, and date ranges. Customers use this to view their order history with item-level details, while sellers use it to manage order items requiring fulfillment.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Response includes order item summary information optimized for list displays, including product details, variant information, quantities, prices, and current status.

For customer order history, filter by order ID to retrieve all items in a specific order. For seller fulfillment workflows, filter by seller ID and status to identify items requiring action (paid, shipped, delivered).
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_items table with pagination and filtering.

Apply filters based on request criteria:
- shopping_mall_order_id: filter items belonging to specific order
- shopping_mall_seller_id: filter items for specific seller (seller dashboard)
- status: filter by item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)
- created_at range: filter by order date range

Join with shopping_mall_products for product name and image, shopping_mall_product_variants for option values, shopping_mall_orders for order number.

For customer access: validate customer owns the order (via shopping_mall_orders.customer_id).
For seller access: validate seller ID matches authenticated seller.
For admin access: allow unrestricted queries.

Return cursor-based pagination with sortable fields: created_at, status, price.
Default sort: created_at DESC (newest first).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order items

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete order item details including the purchased quantity, unit price at time of purchase, current item status, and references to the associated product, product variant, and seller. The response includes all information needed to display order item details to customers or manage fulfillment for sellers.

Order items maintain independent status tracking (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) to support individual item cancellation and refund workflows. The price is snapshotted at purchase time to preserve the transaction state regardless of subsequent product price changes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_items table by primary key UUID.

Join with shopping_mall_products to include product name and details.
Join with shopping_mall_product_variants to include variant SKU code and option values.
Join with shopping_mall_sellers to include seller shop name.

Validate that the requesting user has access to this order item:
- For customers: verify the order item belongs to an order owned by the customer
- For sellers: verify the seller_id matches the authenticated seller
- For administrators: allow access to all order items

Return 404 if order item not found or user lacks access.
Return complete order item entity with related product, variant, and seller information.

responseBody.description: Complete order item details with product, variant, and seller information

operations.description:
Update an order item's status and properties within the order fulfillment workflow.

This operation allows authorized users to modify order item status as it progresses through the purchase lifecycle. Status transitions follow strict business rules: items move from paid to shipped when sellers dispatch products, from shipped to delivered upon customer confirmation, and to cancelled or refunded when cancellation or refund requests are approved.

Administrators can perform force operations to cancel or refund items regardless of current status. Sellers can update status for items from their own products during normal fulfillment. The operation validates all status transitions and automatically triggers inventory adjustments when items are cancelled or refunded.

Returns the complete updated order item including current status, quantity, price, and timestamps. Order item snapshots preserve the state at time of purchase and cannot be modified through this endpoint.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update order item status and properties with business rule validation.

Validate that order item exists and is not soft deleted. Check caller permissions: admin can update any order item, seller can only update items from their products. Validate status transitions according to business rules:
- paid → shipped (seller shipping)
- paid → cancelled (cancellation approved)
- shipped → delivered (delivery confirmation)
- delivered → refunded (refund approved)
- Any → cancelled/refunded (admin force operation)

Reject invalid status transitions with 400 error. Update status, updated_at timestamp. If status becomes cancelled/refunded, trigger automatic inventory restoration by creating positive inventory records. Return updated order item with all fields including snapshot relation.

responseBody.description: Updated order item with all fields and current status

requestBody.description: Order item update data including new status and modifiable fields

prerequisites.description: Order item must be created as part of an order before it can be updated. POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders creates the order and its order items in shopping_mall_order_items table.

operations.description:
Retrieve snapshots of an order item capturing its state at the time of purchase.

This operation returns immutable snapshots that preserve the complete state of the order item including product name, description, variant SKU code, variant price, and seller shop information (name and logo) as they existed when the order was placed. These snapshots ensure accurate historical information for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

Snapshots are created automatically when an order is placed and cannot be modified or deleted. Each order item has exactly one snapshot. The snapshots can be viewed by the customer who placed the order and the seller of the order item. Administrators can view snapshots of any order item on the platform.

This endpoint requires proper authorization - only the order owner (customer) or the seller of the order item can access the snapshots. The orderId parameter establishes the order context, while itemId identifies the specific order item within that order.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table filtered by shopping_mall_order_item_id.

First validate that the order item exists by checking shopping_mall_order_items with the provided itemId and that it belongs to the order specified by orderId.

Verify authorization: the requesting user must be either (1) the customer who placed the order (shopping_mall_orders.customer_id matches authenticated customer), or (2) the seller of the order item (shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_seller_id matches authenticated seller), or (3) an administrator.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to verify the relationship between orderId and itemId.

Return the snapshot record with all fields: id, product_name, product_description, variant_sku_code, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_shop_logo, created_at.

Since each order item has exactly one snapshot (unique constraint), pagination will typically return a single record. Use standard pagination response format for consistency.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order item snapshots

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters

prerequisites.description: Order must be placed before its snapshots can be retrieved. Order creation automatically generates order items and their immutable snapshots capturing product, variant, and seller state at purchase time.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific order item snapshot by its identifier.

This operation returns the immutable snapshot of an order item, preserving the exact state of the product, variant, and seller profile at the time of purchase. Snapshots are created automatically when an order is placed and cannot be modified.

The snapshot includes the product name, description, variant SKU code, variant price, seller shop name, and seller shop logo as they appeared at purchase time. This ensures accurate historical information for dispute resolution, customer support, and audit trail purposes.

The path parameters validate that the snapshot belongs to the specified order and order item, ensuring proper access control and data integrity.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table by snapshot ID.

Validate that the snapshot exists and belongs to the specified order item:
1. Load snapshot by snapshotId
2. Verify snapshot.shopping_mall_order_item_id matches itemId
3. Load order item by itemId
4. Verify order item.shopping_mall_order_id matches orderId
5. Return snapshot if all validations pass

Return 404 if snapshot not found or if hierarchy validation fails (snapshot doesn't belong to specified order/item).

No authorization check in this operation - authorization middleware handles access control (customer can view their own order snapshots, seller can view snapshots for their order items, admin can view any snapshot).

responseBody.description: Complete order item snapshot with preserved product, variant, and seller profile state

prerequisites.description: Order must be created first because order items and their snapshots are automatically generated during order placement - snapshots cannot exist without an order

operations.description:
Retrieve the immutable snapshot of an order item capturing its state at the time of purchase.

This operation returns the historical snapshot preserving the exact product name, description, variant SKU code, price, and seller shop information (name and logo) as they existed when the order was placed. Snapshots are created automatically during checkout and cannot be modified.

Snapshots serve critical purposes for dispute resolution, customer support, and audit compliance. They ensure that order records remain accurate even if the original product is modified, the variant is deleted, or the seller changes their shop profile. The snapshot is permanently linked to the order item and retained indefinitely.

Access is restricted to the customer who placed the order, the seller who fulfilled it, and administrators. Attempting to access snapshots for order items outside these permissions will result in authorization errors.
operations.name: patchByItemid
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table filtering by shopping_mall_order_item_id = {itemId}.

Validate that the requesting user has permission to view this snapshot:
- Customer: must be the owner of the parent order (join shopping_mall_orders to verify customer_id)
- Seller: must be the seller of the order item (verify shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_seller_id matches authenticated seller)
- Administrator: full access

Return 404 if no snapshot exists for the order item (should not occur under normal circumstances as snapshots are created during order placement).

Return snapshot fields: id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, product_name, product_description, variant_sku_code, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_shop_logo, created_at.

Do not allow any modification operations - snapshots are immutable by business rule.

responseBody.description: Complete order item snapshot with preserved product, variant, and seller state at purchase time

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific order item snapshot containing preserved product, variant, and seller information at the time of purchase.

This operation returns immutable historical data capturing the exact state of the purchased item when the order was placed. The snapshot includes the product name and description, variant SKU code and price, and seller shop name and logo as they appeared at purchase time. This ensures accurate transaction records even if the original product, variant, or seller profile has been modified or deleted since the order was placed.

Snapshots are created automatically by the system when an order is placed and cannot be modified. This endpoint is used for order history display, dispute resolution, and audit trail purposes. Customers, sellers, and administrators can access snapshots for order items they have permission to view.
operations.name: getByItemidAndSnapshotid
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table by snapshotId (UUID).

Validate that the snapshot exists and is associated with the provided itemId (shopping_mall_order_item_id).

Verify caller has permission to access the order item:
- Customer: must be the owner of the parent order (join through orderItem → order → customer_id)
- Seller: must be the seller of the order item (check orderItem.shopping_mall_seller_id)
- Administrator/Super Administrator: full access

Return the complete snapshot record including all fields: id, shopping_mall_order_item_id, product_name, product_description, variant_sku_code, variant_price, seller_shop_name, seller_shop_logo, created_at.

Handle 404 if snapshot not found or if itemId/snapshotId mismatch.
Handle 403 if caller lacks permission to access the order item.

responseBody.description: Complete order item snapshot with preserved product, variant, and seller information

operations.description:
Retrieve the variant option values associated with a specific order item snapshot.

This operation returns the product option values (such as Color, Size, Material) that were captured at the time of purchase and preserved in the order item snapshot. Each option value represents one dimension of the purchased variant, enabling accurate reconstruction of what the customer bought.

The snapshot data is immutable and reflects the exact state at purchase time, even if the product or variant has been modified or deleted since. This endpoint supports pagination for variants with many option values.

Access is restricted to the customer who placed the order, the seller who owns the product, and administrators. The orderId, itemId, and snapshotId parameters must correspond to existing entities with proper relationships.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options table filtered by order_item_snapshot_id.

1. Validate orderId exists in shopping_mall_orders table
2. Validate itemId exists in shopping_mall_order_items table and belongs to orderId
3. Validate snapshotId exists in shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots table and belongs to itemId
4. Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options where order_item_snapshot_id = snapshotId
5. Join with shopping_mall_product_option_values to get option value details (value, display order)
6. Join with shopping_mall_product_option_definitions to get option type names (Color, Size, etc.)
7. Apply pagination from request body (page, limit, sort)
8. Return paginated list of variant options with option name and value

Authorization: Verify requester is the order's customer, the product's seller, or an administrator.

Edge cases: Return 404 if orderId, itemId, or snapshotId not found or relationships don't match. Return empty array if snapshot has no variant options (simple product without options).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of variant option values for the order item snapshot

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for variant options list

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific product option value from an order item's snapshot variant options.

This operation returns the details of a single option value (such as Color: Red or Size: Large) that was captured in the order item snapshot at the time of purchase. The snapshot preserves the exact product configuration the customer received, enabling accurate dispute resolution and order history review.

Order item snapshots are immutable records created when an order is placed. They capture the complete state of the product variant including all option values. This endpoint allows customers and sellers to inspect individual option values within that snapshot.

Access is restricted to the customer who placed the order, the seller who fulfilled it, and administrators. The option ID must correspond to an option value actually associated with the order item's snapshot.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options table by optionId.

Validate that the order item snapshot exists and belongs to the specified order and item:
1. Verify orderId matches shopping_mall_orders.id
2. Verify itemId matches shopping_mall_order_items.id
3. Verify the item belongs to the order (shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_order_id = orderId)
4. Get the snapshot ID from shopping_mall_order_item_snapshots where shopping_mall_order_item_id = itemId
5. Verify optionId exists in shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options with order_item_snapshot_id matching the snapshot

Authorization: Allow access if requester is the customer who placed the order, the seller of the product, or an administrator.

Join with shopping_mall_product_option_values to return option value details (name, display order).
Return 404 if order, item, snapshot, or option not found.
Return 403 if requester lacks permission to view this order item.

Retrieve a paginated list of product option values associated with an order item snapshot.

This operation returns the exact option combination (such as Color, Size, Material) that was captured at the time of purchase. Each record represents one option value assigned to the order item snapshot, enabling normalized querying of variant configurations.

Order item snapshots are immutable audit trail records that preserve the complete product state at purchase time for dispute resolution and historical reference. The variant options cannot be modified and are retained indefinitely even after the original product or variant is deleted.

Results support pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Each option value includes the option definition name (e.g., "Color") and the specific value (e.g., "Red").
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options table filtered by order_item_snapshot_id.

1. Validate that the order item snapshot exists and belongs to the authenticated user (customer who placed the order, seller of the product, or administrator).
2. Join with shopping_mall_product_option_values to retrieve option value details.
3. Join with shopping_mall_product_option_definitions through product_option_values to include option name (e.g., "Color", "Size").

5. Apply optional sorting by option name or value.
6. Return paginated list with option definition name, option value, and timestamps.

Edge cases: Return empty array if no variant options exist (product had no options). Handle soft-deleted option values by including them in historical snapshots.

Retrieve a specific product option value from an order item snapshot.

This operation returns the details of a single variant option (such as Color=Red or Size=Large) that was part of the product variant purchased in an order item. The option value is retrieved from the shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options junction table, which captures the exact option combination at the time of purchase.

The snapshot data is immutable and permanently preserved, referencing the shopping_mall_product_option_values table to provide the option value name. This ensures accurate historical reconstruction of the purchased product configuration for dispute resolution, order verification, and audit trail purposes.

The endpoint validates that the snapshot belongs to the specified order item before returning the option details, ensuring data integrity and preventing access to unrelated snapshot records.

Query shopping_mall_order_item_snapshot_variant_options table by primary key id (optionId parameter).

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shipments for the authenticated seller.

This operation provides sellers with the ability to search and browse their shipments using various criteria including tracking number, shipping date range, and delivery confirmation status. The endpoint supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

Sellers can filter shipments by tracking carrier, shipping date ranges, and confirmation status. The response includes shipment summary information optimized for list displays, including tracking details and item counts.

Authentication required: seller actor. Returns only shipments belonging to the authenticated seller.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_shipments table with pagination and filtering. Filter by seller_id from authenticated user context. Apply search filters on tracking_carrier, tracking_number (partial match), shipped_at date range, and confirmed_at status. Join with shopping_mall_shipment_items to count items per shipment. Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Sort by shipped_at descending by default. Validate seller authentication before query execution.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering shipments

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific shipment including tracking information and associated order items.

This operation returns complete shipment details including the shipping carrier name, tracking number, shipped date, and delivery confirmation status. The response includes all order items contained in this shipment, allowing customers and sellers to view which items are being delivered together.

Shipments are created by sellers when they ship order items. All items in a shipment share the same tracking information and delivery confirmation status. Customers can confirm delivery for the entire shipment, or items automatically confirm as delivered after 14 days from the shipping date.

The shipment must exist and not be soft-deleted. Access is restricted to the seller who created the shipment or the customer who placed the order containing the shipment's items.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_shipments table by primary key (UUID). Join with shopping_mall_shipment_items to retrieve associated order items. For each shipment item, join with shopping_mall_order_items to include order item details (product, variant, quantity, price, status). Include seller information from the shipment record. Validate that the shipment exists and deleted_at is null. Return 404 if shipment not found. Authorization check: allow access only to the shipment's seller or the customer who owns the order containing the shipment items.

responseBody.description: Complete shipment details with tracking information and associated order items

operations.description:
Create a new shipment for order items purchased from a seller.

This operation allows sellers to create shipments for their order items that have paid status. The seller selects one or more order items to include in the shipment and provides tracking information including the carrier name and tracking number. All order items included in the shipment must belong to the same seller and have paid status.

When a shipment is created, all order items included in that shipment automatically change to shipped status. Different sellers always ship separately, meaning each seller creates their own shipments for their respective items. Order items from different sellers cannot be combined into a single shipment.

The shipment serves as the delivery record linking the seller's package to the customer's order items. Customers can later confirm delivery for the shipment, which marks all items in the shipment as delivered.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shipment record in shopping_mall_shipments table with seller_id (from authenticated seller), tracking_carrier, tracking_number, shipped_at (current timestamp), and confirmed_at (null initially).

For each orderItemId in the request:
1. Verify the order item exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (shopping_mall_order_items.shopping_mall_seller_id matches)
2. Verify the order item status is 'paid' (not shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded)
3. Verify the order item is not already assigned to another shipment (no existing record in shopping_mall_shipment_items)
4. Create a shopping_mall_shipment_items record linking shipment_id to order_item_id

After all shipment items are created, update all included order items' status to 'shipped' in a single transaction.

Validate that all order items belong to the same seller (enforced by step 1). If any validation fails, rollback the entire transaction and return appropriate error.

Return the complete shipment object including all shipment items with their order item details.

responseBody.description: Complete shipment object with tracking information and included order items

requestBody.description: Shipment creation data including order items to ship and tracking information

prerequisites.description: Order must be created with order items before seller can ship those items. Order items are generated during checkout and must exist with 'paid' status to be included in a shipment.

operations.description:
Update tracking information for an existing shipment.

This operation allows sellers to modify the tracking carrier and tracking number for a shipment they own. This is typically used when a seller needs to correct tracking information or update it after initially creating the shipment.

Only the seller who owns the shipment can update it. The shipment must not yet be confirmed by the customer. Once delivery is confirmed, tracking information becomes immutable. All order items in the shipment share the same tracking information, so updating the shipment automatically applies to all contained items.

The tracking number must be unique across all shipments in the system. If the provided tracking number already exists for another shipment, the update will be rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the authenticated seller owns the shipment by checking seller_id matches authenticated seller ID.

Verify shipment is not yet confirmed (confirmed_at is null). If already confirmed, reject with 403 Forbidden.

Validate tracking_number uniqueness by querying shopping_mall_shipments table excluding current shipment ID.

Update tracking_carrier and tracking_number fields in shopping_mall_shipments table.

Update updated_at timestamp to current time.

Return the complete updated shipment entity including all fields.

operations.description:
Create a new product review for a purchased and delivered order item.

This operation allows customers to submit reviews for products they have purchased and received. Each review requires a star rating from 1 to 5 stars and optionally includes text content describing the customer's experience. The review is automatically associated with the customer, the product being reviewed, and the order from which the purchase was made.

The system enforces a constraint of one review per product per order, preventing duplicate reviews for the same purchase. Reviews can only be created after the associated order item status is "delivered". The created review appears on the product detail page and contributes to the product's average rating calculation.

Authentication is required - only the customer who placed the order can create a review for that order's items.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new review record in shopping_mall_reviews table.

1. Validate request body:
   - rating must be integer between 1 and 5
   - content is optional, can be null or string
   - customer_id, product_id, order_id must be valid UUIDs

2. Verify prerequisites:
   - Check that the order item associated with (order_id, product_id) has status "delivered"
   - Verify no existing review exists with same [customer_id, product_id, order_id] combination (unique constraint)
   - Confirm customer_id matches the authenticated user's customer ID

3. Insert review record:
   - Generate UUID for id
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to null
   - Persist to shopping_mall_reviews table

4. Return the created review entity with all fields.

5. Error handling:
   - 400 if rating out of range or invalid UUID format
   - 403 if customer attempts to review an order they don't own
   - 409 if review already exists for this product/order combination
   - 422 if order item is not yet delivered

responseBody.description: The newly created review entity with all fields including generated id and timestamps.

This operation allows customers to modify their own reviews after submission. Customers can update the star rating (1-5 stars) and/or the review text content. The rating field is required and must be between 1 and 5 stars. The content field is optional, allowing customers to submit rating-only reviews or add text to existing reviews.

Every review edit automatically creates a snapshot that preserves the previous rating and text content before the update. These snapshots are used for audit trails and dispute resolution, and remain accessible even if the review is later deleted.

Only the customer who authored the review can update it. Attempts to update another customer's review will be rejected. The review must exist and not be deleted.

Update the shopping_mall_reviews record identified by reviewId.

1. Verify the review exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)

3. Validate rating is between 1 and 5
4. Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_review_snapshots table preserving the current rating and content values before update
5. Update the review's rating and content fields
6. Update the updated_at timestamp to current time
7. Return the updated review entity

Edge cases:
- Review not found: return 404
- Not the review author: return 403
- Review already deleted: return 404
- Invalid rating (outside 1-5): return 400

This operation allows customers to remove their review content from public display on the product detail page. When a review is deleted, the review content and rating are no longer visible to other users and are excluded from the product's average rating calculation.

The review is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp. All review snapshots created during previous edits remain preserved in the system for administrative review and dispute resolution purposes. The deletion is permanent from the customer's perspective - the review cannot be restored.

Customers can only delete their own reviews. Attempts to delete reviews written by other customers will be rejected. This operation does not affect the customer's ability to write new reviews for other orders of the same product.

operations.specification:
Delete a review by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current time.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify the authenticated customer is the author of the review by comparing customer_id with the authenticated user's ID
2. If the customer does not own the review, reject with 403 Forbidden
3. If the review is already deleted, reject with 404 Not Found
4. Update the review's deleted_at field to the current timestamp
5. Recalculate the product's average rating excluding all deleted reviews
6. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Review does not exist: return 404 Not Found
- Customer not authorized (review belongs to another customer): return 403 Forbidden
- Review already deleted: return 404 Not Found

No request body required for DELETE operation. No response body required per REST conventions.

Only order items with paid status can be cancelled. Items with shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded status will be rejected. Each cancellation request targets one order item and does not affect other items in the same order.

Upon successful creation, the cancellation request enters pending status and awaits seller approval or rejection. The seller can respond to the request, which creates a snapshot of the request state at the time of response.

1. Validate the order item exists and has status 'paid'. Reject if status is shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.
2. Verify the authenticated customer is the owner of the order (via order's customer_id).
3. Check that no active cancellation request already exists for this order item (status = pending).
4. Create cancellation request with: shopping_mall_order_item_id = orderItemId, shopping_mall_customer_id = authenticated user's ID, reason = from request body, status = 'pending', created_at = now, updated_at = now.
5. Return the created cancellation request with full details.

Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots capturing the status, reason, response_reason, and timestamp. If approved, update the order item status to cancelled and create an inventory record with positive quantity to restore stock. Return the updated cancellation request entity. operations.description:
Submit a request to become an administrator on the platform.

This operation allows any authenticated user, whether a customer or seller, to apply for administrator access. The request must include a reason text explaining why the user wants to become an administrator. Upon submission, the request enters a pending state awaiting review by super administrators.

The system automatically determines the applicant type from the authenticated session. Each user can have only one pending promotion request at a time. If a user submits a new request while a previous one is still pending, the previous pending request is automatically cancelled.

Once submitted, super administrators can review the request and either approve it (granting administrator access) or reject it with a reason. The requesting user can view the status of their request through the detail endpoint.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new administrator promotion request for the authenticated user.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract authenticated user ID and session ID from request context (customer or seller)
2. Determine actor_type based on user type ('customer' or 'seller')
3. Validate reason field: must be non-empty string
4. Check for existing pending request by the same user
5. If pending request exists, cancel it (set status to 'rejected' or soft delete) before creating new one
6. Create new shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests record with:
   - actor_type: determined from user type
   - reason: from request body
   - status: 'pending'
   - created_at: current timestamp
7. Create corresponding subtype record:
   - For customers: shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_customers with customer_id and customer_session_id
   - For sellers: shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers with seller_id and seller_session_id
8. Return the created promotion request entity

Validation:
- Reason must be non-empty (trim and check length > 0)
- User must be authenticated (customer or seller session required)
- Only one pending request allowed per user at a time

Error handling:
- 400: Empty or missing reason
- 401: Not authenticated
- Return created entity on success

operations.description:
Update an administrator promotion request by changing its approval status.

This operation allows super administrators to review and respond to pending administrator promotion requests. The super administrator can approve the request, granting the user administrator access, or reject it with a required explanation.

When a request is approved, the requesting user (customer or seller) is granted regular administrator privileges. When rejected, the rejection reason is recorded and visible to the user. The operation creates an audit snapshot preserving the decision details.

Only super administrators can access this endpoint. Attempting to update a request that is no longer in pending status (already approved or rejected) will be rejected.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the admin promotion request status by requestId UUID.

1. Verify the requesting user is a super administrator via session token
2. Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests by id
3. Validate request exists and status is 'pending' - reject if already approved/rejected
4. Validate status transition: only 'approved' or 'rejected' allowed
5. If status is 'rejected', validate rejection_reason is provided and non-empty
6. Update the request: set status, rejection_reason (if rejected), updated_at timestamp
7. Create audit snapshot in shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots:
   - Link to request id
   - Set responding_super_administrator_id to current super admin
   - Capture actor_type, new status, reason (rejection_reason for rejected)
   - Set created_at timestamp
8. If approved, trigger administrator account creation/upgrade for the requesting user
9. Return the updated full request entity

Edge cases:
- Request not found: 404
- Not pending status: 409 Conflict
- Missing rejection_reason for rejected status: 400 Bad Request
- Non-super-admin caller: 403 Forbidden

The endpoint supports date range filtering and status-based queries to help sellers efficiently manage their order pipeline.

Supports filtering by status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), order ID, and date ranges. Response includes order item summary information with product details, variant information, quantities, prices, and current status optimized for list displays.
