Update a cancellation request by responding to it as a seller.

This operation allows sellers to approve or reject customer cancellation requests for order items. When responding, the seller must provide a response reason explaining the approval or rejection decision. The operation validates that the cancellation request exists and is in pending status.

Upon successful response, the system creates an immutable snapshot preserving the request state at the time of response for audit trail and dispute resolution. If approved, the order item status changes to cancelled and inventory is automatically restored via inventory records.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate the cancellation request exists and is in pending status. Verify the seller has permission to respond (seller owns the order item associated with the cancellation request). Update the cancellation request status to approved or rejected. Set the response_reason field with the seller's explanation. Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots capturing the request state, seller ID, status, reason, and response reason. If status is approved, update the associated order item status to cancelled and create an inventory record with positive quantity to restore stock. Return the updated cancellation request entity.

responseBody.description: Updated cancellation request with seller response

requestBody.description: Seller's response to the cancellation request with approval status and reason

prerequisites.description: Order must be created before cancellation requests can be made for its items
Cancellation request must exist before seller can respond to it with approval or rejection

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of refund requests for order items.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for refund requests including status filtering (pending, approved, rejected), date range filtering by request submission date, and actor-specific filtering. Customers can view their own refund requests, while sellers can view refund requests for order items they sold.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting by request date. Response includes refund request summary information optimized for list displays, including order item details, request status, and timestamps.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_refund_requests table with pagination and filtering.

Apply filters based on authenticated actor:
- Customers: filter by customer_id = authenticated customer
- Sellers: filter by seller_id = authenticated seller (via orderItems relationship)
- Administrators: no filter (can view all)

Support status filtering (pending, approved, rejected), requested_at date range filtering, and order item status filtering via join with shopping_mall_order_items.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to include product and variant information in response.
Join with shopping_mall_customers for customer display name.
Join with shopping_mall_sellers for seller shop name.

Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets.
Sort by requested_at descending (newest first) by default.

Validate that refund requests are only visible to authorized actors (request owner customer, responsible seller, or administrators).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund request summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for refund requests

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific refund request.

This operation returns the complete refund request record including the customer's reason, current status (pending, approved, or rejected), seller's response reason if responded, and all relevant timestamps. The refund request is associated with a specific order item and can only be accessed by authorized parties: the customer who submitted the request, the seller who owns the order item, or administrators.

Refund requests are created for individual order items with delivered status within 7 days of delivery. The response includes the full refund request state to support customer tracking of their refund status and seller review of pending requests.

Returns 404 if the refund request does not exist or the caller lacks authorization to access it.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_refund_requests table by primary key UUID.

Authorization checks:
- Allow access if caller is the customer who submitted the request (customer_id matches)
- Allow access if caller is the seller who owns the order item (join order_items to get seller_id, compare with caller)
- Allow access if caller is administrator or superAdministrator
- Return 404 if not found or unauthorized (do not reveal existence to unauthorized users)

Join with shopping_mall_order_items to include order item context if needed for authorization.
Include related snapshot records if caller needs audit trail (optional expansion).

Return full refund request entity with all fields: id, order_item_id, customer_id, seller_id, reason, status, response_reason, requested_at, responded_at, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: Complete refund request details including customer reason, status, seller response, and timestamps

operations.description:
Respond to a customer's refund request by approving or rejecting it with a response reason.

This operation allows sellers to review and respond to refund requests submitted by customers for delivered order items. Sellers must provide a response reason explaining their approval or rejection decision.

When a seller responds to a refund request, the system creates an immutable snapshot preserving the request state at the time of response. If approved, the order item status changes to refunded and stock quantity is restored through an inventory record. If rejected, the order item remains in delivered status.

Only sellers can respond to refund requests for their own order items. Refund requests must be in pending status to be responded to.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Validate refund request exists and is in pending status. Verify the authenticated seller is the owner of the order item associated with this refund request. Update status to approved or rejected based on request body. Set response_reason, seller_id, and responded_at timestamp. Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots preserving the state at response time. If status is approved: update the order item status to refunded, create an inventory record with positive quantity change to restore stock. Return the updated refund request entity. Handle concurrent response attempts with optimistic locking.

responseBody.description: Updated refund request with seller response

requestBody.description: Seller's response to the refund request with approval/rejection decision and reason

prerequisites.description: Refund request must be created by customer before seller can respond to it with approval or rejection

operations.description:
Retrieve seller dashboard statistics and shop summary information.

This operation provides sellers with a comprehensive overview of their shop's current state, including total product count, order item statistics, and pending request counts. The dashboard helps sellers quickly assess their business performance and identify items requiring attention.

Returns aggregated counts for products, order items, pending cancellation requests, and pending refund requests. All counts are scoped to the authenticated seller's account. Optional date range filters can be applied to focus on specific time periods using entity creation timestamps.

Requires seller authentication. Access is restricted to sellers with approved seller approval request status (shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests.status = 'approved').
operations.name: summary
operations.specification:
Query aggregated statistics for the authenticated seller:

1. Count total products from shopping_mall_products where seller_id matches authenticated seller and deleted_at is null
2. Count total order items from shopping_mall_order_items where seller_id matches and deleted_at is null
3. Count pending cancellation requests from shopping_mall_cancellation_requests where status is 'pending' and linked to seller's order items
4. Count pending refund requests from shopping_mall_refund_requests where status is 'pending' and seller_id matches

Apply optional date range filters if provided in request body. Join with order_items table to filter cancellation requests by seller's items. Return single dashboard summary object with all counts.

responseBody.description: Seller dashboard summary with aggregated statistics counts

requestBody.description: Optional filter criteria for dashboard statistics including date range boundaries

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete category hierarchy as a tree structure for browsing and navigation.

This operation returns all active categories organized in a two-level hierarchical structure. Top-level categories are returned with their associated subcategories nested within. Each category includes its identifier, name, and description for display purposes.

The tree structure enables customers to navigate the product classification system efficiently. Parent categories appear at the root level with their subcategories nested as children arrays. Only active categories (not soft-deleted) are included in the response.

This endpoint is accessible to all authenticated users for product discovery and browsing. The hierarchical format matches the UI requirements for category navigation components.
operations.name: tree
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_categories table for all active categories (deleted_at IS NULL).

Build hierarchical tree structure:
1. Fetch all top-level categories (parent_id IS NULL)
2. For each top-level category, fetch its direct subcategories (parent_id = category.id)
3. Nest subcategories within parent's children array
4. Return only two levels (subcategories cannot have their own children per business rules)

Include fields: id, parent_id, name, description for each category.
Sort categories by created_at or name for consistent ordering.
Ensure soft-deleted categories (deleted_at NOT NULL) are excluded from results.

No authentication required beyond basic user session - accessible to customers and administrators.

responseBody.description: Hierarchical tree of categories with parent categories containing nested subcategories

operations.description:
Search and filter products from the shopping mall catalog with advanced criteria.

This operation enables customers to discover products through comprehensive search capabilities including text search by product name, category filtering (including subcategories), price range filtering, and in-stock availability filtering. Multiple filters can be applied simultaneously using AND logic.

Results support flexible sorting options including newest first (default), price from low to high, and price from high to low. Only active products (not soft-deleted) are included in search results. Products must have at least one variant to appear as purchasable.

The response includes product summary information optimized for listing displays, containing the main image, name, price or price range, seller shop name, and average rating. Pagination is supported for large result sets.
operations.name: search
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_products table with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

Filtering logic:
- Search term: Apply text search on product name using gin_trgm_ops index
- Category: Filter by category_id, include products from subcategories (recursive query on parent_id)
- Price range: Filter base_price >= minPrice AND base_price <= maxPrice
- In-stock: Exclude products where ALL variants have zero stock (join with shopping_mall_product_variants and inventory_records, calculate cumulative stock)
- Exclude soft-deleted: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Sorting:
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC (default)
- 'priceAsc': ORDER BY base_price ASC
- 'priceDesc': ORDER BY base_price DESC

Join with shopping_mall_sellers for seller shop_name from profile.
Join with shopping_mall_product_images to get first image (display_order = 0) as main image.
Calculate price range from variants if price_override exists.
Calculate average rating from shopping_mall_reviews.

Return cursor-based pagination with IPageIShoppingMallProduct.ISummary response type.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summaries matching search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria including text search, category filter, price range, stock filter, sorting, and pagination

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive analytics and performance metrics for a specific product.

This operation aggregates sales data from the shopping_mall_order_items table and review statistics from the shopping_mall_reviews table to provide sellers and administrators with insights into product performance. The analytics include total units sold, revenue generated, review count, and average rating.

Sellers can access analytics for their own products to monitor sales performance and customer satisfaction. Administrators can access analytics for any product on the platform for oversight and reporting purposes. The data is calculated from historical order items and review records associated with the product.

Product analytics help sellers make informed decisions about inventory management, pricing strategies, and product improvements. The metrics reflect all transactions and reviews associated with the product throughout its lifecycle, excluding cancelled and refunded order items from sales calculations.
operations.name: analytics
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_products table to verify product exists and retrieve basic product information.

For sales metrics:
- Aggregate orderItems where shopping_mall_product_id = productId
- Sum quantity across all order items for total units sold
- Sum (quantity * price) for total revenue
- Filter by status to exclude cancelled/refunded items if business rules require

For review metrics:
- Aggregate reviews where product_id = productId and deleted_at IS NULL
- Count total reviews
- Calculate average rating (AVG of rating field)
- Handle case where no reviews exist (return 0 or null)

Authorization: Verify requesting user is either the product's seller or an administrator.

Return IShoppingMallProduct.IAnalytics with all computed metrics.

Edge cases:
- Product not found: return 404
- Product deleted: return 404 or include in analytics with deleted flag
- No order items: return 0 for sales metrics
- No reviews: return 0 for review count, null or 0 for average rating

responseBody.description: Product analytics including sales metrics and review statistics

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of products with low stock levels requiring seller attention.

This operation aggregates inventory records across all variants of each product to calculate current stock levels. Products are included in the results when their total stock quantity falls below the specified threshold. The response includes product identification information, current stock quantity, and the low-stock threshold for context.

This endpoint is designed for seller dashboard use cases, enabling sellers to quickly identify products that need restocking. Results are paginated to handle large product catalogs efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_products table joined with shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_inventory_records.

For each product, sum all quantity_change values from inventory records across all variants to calculate current stock level.

Filter products where total stock quantity is less than the threshold parameter from request body.

Only include products owned by the authenticated seller (filter by seller_id from session).

Exclude soft-deleted products (deleted_at IS NULL).

Apply pagination with limit and offset from request body.

Sort by stock quantity ascending (lowest stock first) by default.

Return product id, name, sku_codes of variants, current_stock quantity, and threshold used.

Handle edge case: products with no inventory records have zero stock.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of products with low stock summaries

requestBody.description: Low stock threshold and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve the current stock quantity and availability status for a specific product variant.

This operation calculates the real-time stock level by summing all inventory record quantity changes for the variant. The response includes the computed stock quantity and an out-of-stock indicator that determines whether the variant can be added to shopping carts.

Variants with zero or negative stock are marked as out of stock and cannot be purchased. This endpoint is used by customers during product browsing and by sellers for inventory monitoring.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_inventory_records table filtering by product_variant_id. Sum all quantity_change values to calculate current stock. Return stock quantity and isOutOfStock boolean (true when stock <= 0). Validate that the variant exists and belongs to the specified product. Include soft-deleted variant check - return 404 if variant is deleted. No joins needed beyond variant existence verification. Stock calculation is a simple SUM aggregation on the inventory records table.

responseBody.description: Current stock quantity and availability status for the variant

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before variants can be added to it
Product variant must be created before its stock quantity can be retrieved

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of customer reviews for a specific product.

This operation returns all non-deleted reviews for the specified product, sorted by newest first (most recently created or edited reviews at the top). Each review includes the rating (1-5 stars), optional text content, creation timestamp, and customer information.

Reviews are only visible if they have not been deleted by their authors. The response includes pagination metadata to support browsing large review sets. This endpoint is publicly accessible to all customers viewing the product detail page.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_reviews table filtering by product_id and excluding deleted records (deleted_at IS NULL). Join with shopping_mall_customers to include customer display name. Order by created_at DESC to show newest reviews first. Apply cursor-based pagination with configurable page size. Calculate average rating from all non-deleted reviews for the product and include in response metadata. Return 404 if product does not exist.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product review summaries with metadata

parameters.description: Product UUID to retrieve reviews for
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Pagination and sorting parameters for review list

operations.description:
Retrieve the average rating and total review count for a specific product.

This operation returns the aggregated rating information for a product, including the average rating calculated from all non-deleted reviews and the total count of reviews. The average rating is computed by summing all rating values from non-deleted reviews and dividing by the count of non-deleted reviews.

If a product has no non-deleted reviews, the average rating will be null. Deleted reviews are excluded from both the average calculation and the total count. This ensures the displayed rating reflects current customer sentiment.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_reviews table filtering by product_id and excluding soft-deleted reviews (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Calculate average rating using AVG(rating) function on non-deleted reviews. Count total non-deleted reviews using COUNT(*). Return null for averageRating if no reviews exist. Join with shopping_mall_products to verify product exists. Handle case where product has no reviews by returning averageRating as null and totalReviews as 0.

responseBody.description: Product rating information including average rating and review count

operations.description:
Retrieve the seller's shop dashboard summary statistics.

This operation provides a quick overview of the seller's shop performance and pending tasks. The summary includes the total number of products listed, total order items across all products, count of pending cancellation requests awaiting seller response, and count of pending refund requests awaiting seller response.

This endpoint is designed for the seller dashboard home page, giving sellers an at-a-glance view of their shop status and actionable items requiring attention.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query dashboard statistics for the authenticated seller.

1. Count total products owned by the seller from shopping_mall_products table
2. Count total order items referencing the seller's products from shopping_mall_order_items table
3. Count pending cancellation requests where seller has not yet responded from shopping_mall_cancellation_requests table
4. Count pending refund requests where seller has not yet responded from shopping_mall_refund_requests table
5. Return aggregated statistics as a single summary object

Ensure seller authentication is validated before querying. All counts should be current as of query time.

responseBody.description: Seller dashboard summary statistics

operations.description:
Approve a pending administrator promotion request, granting the requesting user regular administrator access.

This operation allows super administrators to review and approve administrator promotion requests submitted by customers or sellers. When a request is approved, the requesting user is granted regular administrator privileges with standard administrative capabilities.

The request status changes from pending to approved, and the response timestamp is recorded. The requesting user is notified of the approval decision. Only super administrators can perform this operation; regular administrators cannot approve promotion requests.

Attempting to approve a request that is no longer pending (already approved or rejected) will result in an error.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification: Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests table by requestId UUID. Verify the request status is 'pending' - reject if status is 'approved' or 'rejected'. Verify the authenticated user is a super administrator - reject if regular administrator or other role. Update the request status to 'approved'. Record the response timestamp in updated_at field. Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots with status 'approved' and responding_super_administrator_id. If the requesting user is a customer, create a new administrator account in shopping_mall_administrators with the customer's email. Return the updated promotion request entity. Handle concurrent approval attempts with optimistic locking.

responseBody.description: The approved administrator promotion request entity

operations.description:
Reject an administrator promotion request submitted by a user.

This operation allows super administrators to deny a pending administrator promotion request. When rejecting, the super administrator must provide a rejection reason explaining why the request was denied. The rejection reason is recorded and becomes visible to the requesting user.

Upon successful rejection, the request status changes from 'pending' to 'rejected' and the rejection timestamp is recorded. The requesting user is notified of the decision. Only super administrators can perform this operation; regular administrators do not have permission to reject admin promotion requests.

If the request is no longer pending (already approved or rejected), the operation will fail with an appropriate error response.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification: Validate that the requesting user is a super administrator. Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests by requestId. Verify the request status is 'pending' - reject if already approved or rejected. Update the record: set status to 'rejected', set rejection_reason to the provided value, update updated_at timestamp. Create a snapshot record in shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots capturing the rejected state, responding super administrator ID, actor type, and rejection reason. Return the updated promotion request entity. Handle concurrent modification conflicts with optimistic locking.

responseBody.description: The rejected administrator promotion request with updated status and rejection reason

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator promotion request (UUID format)
parameters.name: requestId

requestBody.description: Rejection details including the reason for denying the promotion request

prerequisites.description: Customer must submit an administrator promotion request before it can be rejected by a super administrator
Seller must submit an administrator promotion request before it can be rejected by a super administrator

operations.description:
Promote a regular administrator to super administrator grade.

This operation allows super administrators to elevate a regular administrator's grade to super administrator, granting them full system oversight capabilities including the ability to manage administrator grades, approve promotion requests, and demote other super administrators.

Upon successful promotion, the administrator immediately gains all super administrator privileges. An audit trail record is created in the administrator grade changes table documenting the transition, the performing super administrator, and the timestamp.

This operation is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators cannot access this endpoint. The promoting super administrator cannot promote themselves through this endpoint.
operations.name: promote
operations.specification:
Verify the requesting user is a super administrator through session authentication.

Query shopping_mall_administrators table by the provided administratorId UUID.

Validate the administrator exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null).

Validate the administrator is currently a regular administrator (not already a super administrator).

Create a new record in shopping_mall_administrator_grade_changes table with:
- shopping_mall_administrator_id: the promoted administrator's ID
- shopping_mall_super_administrator_id: the performing super administrator's ID
- previous_grade: 'administrator'
- new_grade: 'super_administrator'
- reason: optional if provided
- created_at: current timestamp

Update the administrator's grade status in the system (implementation depends on grade storage mechanism).

Return the updated administrator entity with super administrator privileges.

Handle edge cases:
- Administrator not found: return 404
- Administrator already super administrator: return 400
- Requesting user not super administrator: return 403
- Attempting self-promotion through alternative means: validate and reject

responseBody.description: The promoted administrator entity with updated super administrator privileges

parameters.description: UUID of the administrator to promote to super administrator grade
parameters.name: administratorId

operations.description:
Demote a super administrator to regular administrator grade.

This operation allows super administrators to demote other super administrators to regular administrator status. When demoted, the administrator loses super administrator capabilities and retains only regular administrator privileges including seller management, category management, product oversight, order oversight, and user management.

The operation enforces a critical security constraint: super administrators cannot demote themselves. This prevents the system from losing all super administrator access. At least one super administrator must remain in the system at all times.

Upon successful demotion, the grade change is recorded in the administrator grade changes audit trail with the previous grade (super_administrator), new grade (administrator), and optional reason. The affected administrator's permissions are immediately updated to reflect regular administrator capabilities only.
operations.name: demote
operations.specification:
Verify the calling user is a super administrator. Reject if the caller is a regular administrator.

Validate that the administratorId parameter exists and references a valid administrator account. Reject with 404 if not found.

CRITICAL: Check if the administratorId matches the calling super administrator's ID. If attempting self-demotion, reject with 403 Forbidden error with message indicating self-demotion is prohibited.

Verify the target administrator currently has super_administrator grade. If already a regular administrator, reject with 400 Bad Request indicating the administrator is not a super administrator.

Verify that demoting this administrator will not leave the system with zero super administrators. Query the count of super administrators; if count equals 1 (only this target), reject with 400 Bad Request indicating at least one super administrator must remain.

Begin database transaction:
1. Update the administrator's grade from 'super_administrator' to 'administrator'
2. Create a new shopping_mall_administrator_grade_changes record with:
   - shopping_mall_administrator_id: target administrator ID
   - shopping_mall_super_administrator_id: calling super administrator ID
   - previous_grade: 'super_administrator'
   - new_grade: 'administrator'
   - reason: from request body (optional)
   - created_at: current timestamp
3. Commit transaction

Return the updated administrator entity with the new grade reflected.

Handle concurrent demotion attempts with optimistic locking or transaction isolation to prevent race conditions that could leave the system without super administrators.

responseBody.description: The demoted administrator entity with updated grade information

parameters.description: UUID of the administrator to demote (must be a super administrator, cannot be the calling user)
parameters.name: administratorId

requestBody.description: Optional reason for the demotion

operations.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated user's administrator promotion request.

This operation returns the promotion request submitted by the currently logged-in user (either customer or seller). The response includes the request status (pending, approved, or rejected), the reason text provided during submission, and if rejected, the rejection reason provided by the super administrator.

Returns 404 Not Found if the user has never submitted a promotion request. Users can submit a new request after a previous request was rejected.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests table filtered by the authenticated user's ID.

Determine actor_type from authentication context (customer or seller). Join with shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_customers or shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers based on actor_type to filter by user ID.

Return the full promotion request entity including id, actor_type, reason, status, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at.

If no request exists for this user, return 404 Not Found.

Ensure soft-deleted requests (deleted_at not null) are excluded from results.

responseBody.description: The user's administrator promotion request details

operations.description:
Retrieve the current authenticated user's administrator promotion request.

This operation returns the promotion request submitted by the currently logged-in user (either customer or seller). The response includes the request status (pending, approved, or rejected), the reason text provided during submission, and if rejected, the rejection reason provided by the super administrator.

Returns 404 Not Found if the user has never submitted a promotion request. Users can submit a new request after a previous request was rejected.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_admin_promotion_requests table filtered by the authenticated user's ID.

Determine actor_type from authentication context (customer or seller). Join with shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_customers or shopping_mall_admin_promotion_request_of_sellers based on actor_type to filter by user ID.

Return the full promotion request entity including id, actor_type, reason, status, rejection_reason, created_at, updated_at.

If no request exists for this user, return 404 Not Found.

Ensure soft-deleted requests (deleted_at not null) are excluded from results.

responseBody.description: The user's administrator promotion request details

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of orders containing the seller's products for business analytics.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for order data relevant to the seller, including date range filtering, order status filtering, and order number search. Results are sorted by order date with newest orders first by default, supporting pagination for large datasets.

Designed for seller business analytics, this endpoint enables analysis of sales patterns, order trends, and product performance. The query is automatically scoped to orders containing the authenticated seller's products, ensuring data isolation. Response includes order summary information optimized for list displays and analytical processing.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_orders table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters on: order_number (partial match), ordered_at (date range), customer_id, order status (derived from order_items aggregation), seller_id (via order_items join). Support sorting by ordered_at (asc/desc), order_number, total amount.

Join with shopping_mall_order_items for status aggregation and seller filtering. Calculate order total from order_items quantity * price. Implement cursor-based or offset pagination.

Filter by soft-delete status (exclude deleted_at IS NOT NULL unless explicitly requested). Handle edge case: orders with no order items should still be returned if they match other criteria.

Return IPageIShoppingMallOrder.ISummary with pagination metadata (page, limit, total count).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries for analytics

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for order analytics

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of inventory change records for a specific product variant.

This operation provides sellers with complete visibility into their product variant's stock movement history. Each record represents a single inventory change event, whether from manual restocking, adjustments, or automatic updates from orders, cancellations, and refunds.

Supports filtering by date range and reason code, with chronological ordering by timestamp. Response includes quantity change amount, reason categorization, and creation timestamp for each record. The inventory history is read-only and immutable, forming a permanent audit trail for stock level verification and dispute resolution.

Only accessible for variants owned by the authenticated seller. Returns 404 if the variant does not exist or belongs to a different seller.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query shopping_mall_inventory_records table filtered by product_variant_id.

Validate that the variant exists and belongs to the authenticated seller by joining with shopping_mall_product_variants and shopping_mall_products tables.

Apply optional filters from request body: date range (created_at between start and end), reason code matching.

Order results by created_at descending (newest first) for chronological display.

Implement cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size.

Return summary fields: id, quantity_change, reason, created_at.

Handle edge cases: variant not found (404), variant not owned by seller (403), no inventory records (empty array with pagination metadata).

responseBody.description: Paginated list of inventory record summaries showing stock movement history

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering inventory history

authorizations.name: customer
authorizations.description: Registered shoppers who browse products, manage carts, place orders, and write reviews

authorizations.name: seller
authorizations.description: Registered sellers who manage products and inventory, process orders, and handle cancellations/refunds (requires admin approval)

authorizations.name: administrator
authorizations.description: Administrators who manage seller approvals, categories, products, orders, and user accounts

authorizations.name: superAdministrator
authorizations.description: Super administrators who manage administrator promotions/demotions and have full system oversight

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.

IPage.IPagination.description:

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.

IShoppingMallProduct.IAnalytic.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation type with no direct database table mapping. totalUnitsSold: SUM(quantity) from shopping_mall_order_items where product_id matches and status excludes cancelled/refunded items. totalRevenue: SUM(quantity * price) from same filtered order_items. reviewCount: COUNT(*) from shopping_mall_reviews where product_id matches and deleted_at IS NULL. averageRating: AVG(rating) from same filtered reviews, returns null when reviewCount is 0. Authorization: verify requester is product seller or administrator before computing aggregations.

status.description: Approval decision: 'approved' to grant selling privileges, 'rejected' to deny the application. Only pending requests can be updated.
status.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests.status. For update operation, only 'approved' or 'rejected' allowed (transitioning from pending). Server validates status value and sets administrator_id from JWT and reviewed_at timestamp automatically.

rejection_reason.description: Reason for rejection. Required when status is 'rejected', ignored otherwise.

IShoppingMallSellerApprovalRequest.IUpda.description: Request body for reviewing a seller approval request. Administrators use this to approve or reject seller registration applications.
IShoppingMallSellerApprovalRequest.IUpda.x-autobe-specification: Maps to shopping_mall_seller_approval_requests table. Updates: status, rejection_reason. administrator_id set from JWT token. reviewed_at auto-set to current timestamp on update. Business rule: rejection_reason must be non-empty when status='rejected'. Only pending requests can be updated.

products_count.description: Total number of products listed by the seller.
products_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE seller_id = auth.seller.id. Computed at query time.

order_items_count.description: Total number of order items across all seller's products.
order_items_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_order_items JOIN shopping_mall_products ON order_items.product_id = products.id WHERE products.seller_id = auth.seller.id. Computed at query time.

pending_cancellations_count.description: Count of pending cancellation requests awaiting seller response.
pending_cancellations_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_cancellation_requests JOIN shopping_mall_order_items ON cancellation_requests.order_item_id = order_items.id JOIN shopping_mall_products ON order_items.product_id = products.id WHERE products.seller_id = auth.seller.id AND cancellation_requests.responded_at IS NULL. Computed at query time.

pending_refunds_count.description: Count of pending refund requests awaiting seller response.
pending_refunds_count.x-autobe-specification: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_refund_requests JOIN shopping_mall_order_items ON refund_requests.order_item_id = order_items.id JOIN shopping_mall_products ON order_items.product_id = products.id WHERE products.seller_id = auth.seller.id AND refund_requests.responded_at IS NULL. Computed at query time.

IShoppingMallDashboard.ISummary.description: Seller dashboard summary statistics providing an at-a-glance view of shop performance and pending tasks requiring attention.
IShoppingMallDashboard.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation type for seller dashboard. Four COUNT queries: 1) products_count: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_products WHERE seller_id = auth.seller.id, 2) order_items_count: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_order_items JOIN shopping_mall_products ON order_items.product_id = products.id WHERE products.seller_id = auth.seller.id, 3) pending_cancellations_count: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_cancellation_requests JOIN shopping_mall_order_items ON cancellation_requests.order_item_id = order_items.id JOIN shopping_mall_products ON order_items.product_id = products.id WHERE products.seller_id = auth.seller.id AND cancellation_requests.responded_at IS NULL, 4) pending_refunds_count: COUNT(*) FROM shopping_mall_refund_requests JOIN shopping_mall_order_items ON refund_requests.order_item_id = order_items.id JOIN shopping_mall_products ON order_items.product_id = products.id WHERE products.seller_id = auth.seller.id AND refund_requests.responded_at IS NULL. All counts computed at query time for authenticated seller.

averageRating.description: Average star rating for this product calculated from all non-deleted customer reviews. Ranges from 1 to 5 stars. Null when the product has no reviews yet.
averageRating.x-autobe-specification: Computed via AVG(rating) SQL aggregation on shopping_mall_reviews table. Filter: product_id = {productId} AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns null when COUNT of non-deleted reviews is 0. Range: 1.0 to 5.0 when reviews exist.

totalReviews.description: Total number of non-deleted customer reviews for this product. Used alongside averageRating to provide context for the rating's reliability.
totalReviews.x-autobe-specification: Computed via COUNT(*) SQL aggregation on shopping_mall_reviews table. Filter: product_id = {productId} AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns 0 when no non-deleted reviews exist. Always a non-negative integer.

IShoppingMallProductRating.description: Product rating aggregation returned by the product ratings endpoint. Contains the average star rating (1-5 scale) calculated from all non-deleted customer reviews for a specific product, and the total count of non-deleted reviews. averageRating is null when the product has no reviews.
IShoppingMallProductRating.x-autobe-specification: Aggregation DTO computed from shopping_mall_reviews table. Query: SELECT AVG(rating) as averageRating, COUNT(*) as totalReviews FROM shopping_mall_reviews WHERE product_id = {productId} AND deleted_at IS NULL. averageRating is null when no reviews exist (COUNT = 0). totalReviews is 0 when no reviews exist. Join with shopping_mall_products to verify product exists before aggregation. Exclude all soft-deleted reviews from both calculations.

instruction:
Generate comprehensive E2E test suites for the e-commerce shopping mall platform covering:

## Authentication Tests
- Customer signup, login, password change, account deletion
- Seller signup, login, password change, account deletion (with validation)
- Administrator login and access control

## Customer Profile Tests
- Get and update customer profile (display name, phone number)

## Address Management Tests
- Add, update, delete, and set default address
- Multiple addresses per customer

## Seller Approval Tests
- Seller registration submission
- Admin approval/rejection flow
- Rejection reason viewing
- Resubmission after rejection

## Seller Profile Tests
- Get and update seller profile (shop name, description, logo)
- Profile snapshot creation on edits
- Customer viewing seller profiles

## Category Tests
- Admin create/edit/delete categories and subcategories
- Customer browsing categories
- Product listing by category

## Product Management Tests
- Seller create/edit/delete products
- Product snapshot creation on edits
- Product deletion validation (no pending orders/cancellations/refunds)
- Admin product oversight and deletion

## Product Image Tests
- Upload, reorder, and delete product images
- Image changes in snapshots

## Product Variant Tests
- Add/edit/delete variants
- Variant snapshot creation
- Variant deletion validation
- SKU uniqueness

## Inventory Management Tests
- Restock and adjustment operations
- Inventory history tracking
- Stock calculation from inventory records
- Out of stock behavior

## Product Search Tests
- Search by name with pagination
- Filter by category, price range, in-stock
- Sort by newest, price ascending/descending

## Wishlist Tests
- Add/remove products from wishlist
- Wishlist pagination
- Auto-removal when product deleted

## Shopping Cart Tests
- Add variant to cart with quantity
- Combine quantities for same variant
- Update and remove cart items
- Stock warnings and unavailable item marking
- Cart total calculation

## Checkout and Order Tests
- Order review summary
- Payment success/failure handling
- Order creation with stock deduction
- Order item snapshots (product, variant, seller profile)
- Cart cleanup after order

## Order Status Tests
- Order item status transitions (paid → shipped → delivered)
- Order status derivation from items
- Partial completion states

## Shipping and Tracking Tests
- Seller create shipment with tracking
- Multiple items in one shipment
- Customer delivery confirmation
- Auto-delivery after 14 days

## Order Cancellation Tests
- Customer cancellation request (paid items only)
- Seller approve/reject cancellation
- Stock restoration on approval
- Cancellation snapshots

## Refund Request Tests
- Customer refund request (delivered items, within 7 days)
- Seller approve/reject refund
- Stock restoration on approval
- Refund snapshots

## Review Tests
- Create review for delivered products
- One review per product per order validation
- Edit and delete reviews
- Review snapshots
- Average rating calculation

## Seller Dashboard Tests
- Shop summary statistics
- Order items list with status filtering

## Administrator Tests
- Admin request and approval flow
- Admin grade promotion/demotion
- Seller management (approve, reject, suspend, unsuspend)
- Customer management (ban, unban)
- Force cancel/refund orders

## Snapshot Integrity Tests
- Verify snapshots are immutable
- Verify snapshots preserve historical data
- Verify relevant parties can view snapshots

## Edge Cases and Validation
- Account deletion with pending orders
- Product/variant deletion with pending orders
- Cancellation/refund requests outside allowed timeframes
- Stock quantity validations
- Permission and access control validations

scenario.draft: Test successful customer registration with valid email and password credentials. Verify that the system creates a new customer account, generates email verification token, and returns JWT authentication tokens (access and refresh) along with customer profile information. Validate that the customer is automatically authenticated after registration and can immediately access customer features. Check that the response includes customer ID, email, profile details (display name, phone number), account timestamps, and valid token pair with expiration timestamps. This scenario validates the primary registration workflow where a new user joins the platform with unique credentials.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /shoppingMall/auth/customer/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'customer' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'customer' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.

functions.name: test_api_administrator_cart_retrieval_mixed_availability

scenario.draft:
Test administrator cart retrieval when attempting to access a non-existent cart ID.

**Setup**:
1. Authenticate as administrator
2. Generate a valid UUID that does not correspond to any existing cart

**Test Execution**:
1. Administrator calls GET /shoppingMall/administrator/carts/{cartId} with non-existent cart ID
2. Verify system returns 404 Not Found response
3. Verify error message indicates cart was not found
4. Verify no cart data is leaked in the error response

**Business Logic Validation**:
- System properly validates cart existence before returning data
- Non-existent cart IDs result in 404 error (not authorization error)
- Error handling does not expose information about cart existence patterns
- Administrator oversight does not bypass existence validation

scenario.draft:
Test that cart item price snapshot remains consistent after product variant price changes. The test should:

1. Authenticate as a customer via join
2. Create a seller account and product with variants
3. Create a variant with a specific price (e.g., $100)
4. Add the variant to the customer's cart

7. Retrieve the same cart item again using its ID
8. Verify:
   - The cart item's price field remains unchanged (still $100)
   - The price snapshot was captured at time of addition
   - The product variant's current price reflects the update ($150)
   - Cart item shows correct historical pricing for checkout consistency

This validates the business rule that cart items preserve the price at time of addition, ensuring consistent checkout calculation even if variant prices change while items are in the cart.

functions.name: test_api_cart_item_addition_success

scenario.draft:
Test that adding the same product variant multiple times merges quantities instead of creating duplicate cart items.

**Test Steps:**
1. Register a new customer account
2. Register a seller and create a product with one variant
3. Add the variant to cart with quantity 3
4. Add the same variant again with quantity 5
5. Verify the cart contains only ONE cart item for this variant
6. Verify the quantity is 8 (3 + 5), not two separate items

**Validation Points:**
- Only one cart item exists for the variant (no duplicates)
- Quantity is the sum of both addition requests (3 + 5 = 8)
- Price remains the original captured price (not recalculated)
- updated_at timestamp is updated on the second addition
- Cart total_amount reflects merged quantity × price
- Cart items_count remains 1 (not incremented on merge)

scenario.draft:
Test that the cart item captures and preserves the variant's price at time of addition, ensuring consistent pricing even if the variant price changes later.

**Test Steps:**
1. Register a new customer account

- Price snapshot is immutable once captured at addition time
- Merged quantities preserve the original captured price
- Cart total_amount uses captured price, not current variant price
- This ensures checkout calculation consistency regardless of price changes

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path for retrieving variant option values from an order item snapshot. The customer who placed the order should be able to view the product option values (such as Color, Size, Material) that were captured at purchase time.

Test Steps:
1. Register a new seller account via /shoppingMall/auth/seller/join
2. Create a product with option definitions (Color, Size) via /shoppingMall/seller/products and /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/option-definitions
3. Create option values (Red for Color, Large for Size) via /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/option-definitions/{optionDefinitionId}/option-values
4. Create a product variant combining these options via /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants
5. Register a new customer account via /shoppingMall/auth/customer/join
6. Create a shipping address for the customer via /shoppingMall/customer/addresses
7. Add the product variant to the cart via /shoppingMall/customer/cart/items
8. Create an order via /shoppingMall/customer/orders which automatically creates order items, order item snapshots, and variant option junction records
9. Retrieve the variant options for the order item snapshot via the target endpoint

Validation Points:
- Response contains paginated list with correct pagination metadata (current page, limit, total records, total pages)
- Each variant option includes optionName (e.g., 'Color', 'Size'), optionValue (e.g., 'Red', 'Large'), and createdAt timestamp
- The option values match what was configured for the purchased variant at order time
- createdAt timestamp reflects the order placement time (snapshot creation time)
- Verify the snapshot data is immutable by comparing with current variant options (they may differ if variant was edited after purchase)

Business Logic:
- Snapshot preserves exact variant configuration at purchase time per requirements [161], [236], [240], [347]
- Customer can only access snapshots for their own orders
- Variant options are junction records linking order item snapshot to product option values

functions.name: test_api_admin_promotion_request_rejection_with_reason

scenario.draft:
Test that attempting to update an already approved or rejected administrator promotion request returns a conflict error.

**Setup:**
1. Register a super administrator account and authenticate
2. Register a customer account and authenticate
3. Customer submits an administrator promotion request with a valid reason
4. Super administrator approves the request (status changes to 'approved')
5. Use the same request ID for this test

**Test Execution:**
1. Super administrator attempts to call PUT /shoppingMall/superAdministrator/admin-promotion-requests/{requestId} again with status='rejected'
2. Verify the operation is rejected with a conflict error

**Validation Points:**
- Response status is 409 Conflict (not 200 OK)
- The request status remains 'approved' (unchanged)
- Error message indicates the request is no longer in pending status
- No new audit snapshot is created for the invalid transition
- The original approval decision remains intact

**Business Logic:**
- Only pending requests can be updated
- Once a request is approved or rejected, its status is final
- Prevents super administrators from changing decisions after they are made
- Maintains audit trail integrity by preventing status modifications
- This is a business rule validation, not input validation

**Alternative Scenario:**
This test can also be performed with a previously rejected request to verify the same conflict behavior applies to both approved and rejected states.

scenario.draft: Test the seller approval workflow for a customer cancellation request. Scenario: Seller creates a product with variant, customer places an order with the product variant, requests cancellation for the order item (which has paid status), and the seller approves the cancellation request. Validation points: 1) Cancellation request status changes from pending to approved, 2) Order item status changes from paid to cancelled, 3) Inventory record is created with positive quantity to restore stock for the variant, 4) Immutable snapshot is created capturing the request state at time of approval including seller ID, status change, and response reason, 5) Response contains updated cancellation request with approved status. This validates the complete approval workflow including stock restoration and audit trail creation.

functions.name: test_api_cancellation_request_seller_rejection_continues_fulfillment

scenario.draft: Test the business logic validation when seller attempts to respond to a cancellation request that has already been responded to. Scenario: Customer places an order, requests cancellation, seller responds once (approve or reject), then attempts to respond again to the same cancellation request. Validation points: 1) First seller response succeeds and changes status from pending to approved/rejected, 2) Second seller response attempt is rejected with business logic error (not HTTP 400 validation error), 3) Error message indicates the cancellation request has already been responded to, 4) Cancellation request status remains unchanged from the first response, 5) No additional snapshot is created for the failed second attempt. This validates the business rule that cancellation requests can only be responded to once, preventing duplicate responses and maintaining data integrity.

instruction:
Implement complete business logic for the e-commerce shopping mall platform with the following requirements:

## Authentication & Account Management
- Customer signup/login with email/password validation
- Password change with current password verification
- Customer account deletion (soft delete profile, preserve orders and reviews)
- Seller signup/login with approval workflow
- Seller account deletion with validation (no pending orders, no pending cancellation/refund requests)
- Administrator authentication and grade-based access control

## Customer Profile Business Logic
- Profile CRUD with display name and phone number validation
- Profile update creates no snapshot (only seller profiles and products need snapshots)

## Address Management Business Logic
- Multiple addresses per customer with one default
- Address validation (required fields: recipient name, phone, street, city, state, postal code, country)
- Default address setting ensures only one default per customer

## Seller Approval Workflow
- Initial registration creates pending status
- Admin approval changes to approved (can sell)
- Admin rejection stores reason, allows resubmission
- Rejected sellers can submit new registration request

## Seller Profile Business Logic
- Profile CRUD with shop name, description, logo
- Every edit creates immutable snapshot with before/after values
- Snapshots include timestamp and change details

## Category Management
- Hierarchical categories (one level of subcategories)
- Admin-only creation/editing/deletion
- Category deletion sets products to uncategorized (null category_id)

## Product Management
- Product CRUD with required fields (name, description, category_id, base_price)
- Products belong to seller who created them
- Every edit creates product snapshot including all current variants
- Product deletion validation: no pending order items (paid/shipped), no pending cancellation/refund requests
- Deleted products hidden from search/listings but snapshots preserved
- Soft delete with deleted_at timestamp

## Product Image Management
- Multiple images per product with ordering (display_order)
- First image is thumbnail
- Image changes captured in product snapshots
- Image deletion removes from product but preserved in historical snapshots

## Product Variant (SKU) Management
- Variants belong to products with unique SKU per product
- Option values stored as JSON (e.g., {"color": "Red", "size": "Large"})
- Optional price override (if null, use product base price)
- Stock quantity managed via inventory history (not direct field)
- Every edit creates variant snapshot
- Deletion validation: no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund requests
- Products with no variants shown as "unavailable"

## Inventory Management
- Inventory history records track all stock changes
- Each record: variant_id, quantity_change (positive/negative), reason, created_at
- Current stock = SUM of all quantity_change for variant
- Reasons: "restock", "order", "cancellation", "refund", "adjustment"
- Order placement creates negative inventory record
- Cancellation/refund approval creates positive inventory record
- Out of stock (stock <= 0) prevents cart addition

## Product Search & Listing
- Search by product name with pagination
- Filters: category_id (including subcategories), price_min, price_max, in_stock_only
- Sorting: created_at DESC, base_price ASC/DESC
- Listing shows: thumbnail image, name, price/price range, seller shop name, average rating
- Exclude deleted products and suspended sellers

## Wishlist Management
- Customer-product relationship (unique per customer-product pair)
- Pagination support
- Auto-remove when product deleted (cascade or cleanup job)

## Shopping Cart Business Logic
- Customer-variant relationship with quantity
- Adding same variant combines quantities
- Validation: variant exists, not deleted, stock available
- Cart calculation: item subtotals and total
- Mark items as unavailable if variant deleted or out of stock
- Stock warning if cart quantity > available stock

## Checkout & Order Creation
- Order review: items with prices, shipping address, total
- Payment processing simulation (success/failure)
- On payment success:
  - Create order record
  - Create order items (one per variant, with quantity)
  - Create product/variant snapshots for each order item
  - Create seller profile snapshot for each order item
  - Decrease stock (create negative inventory records)
  - Remove items from cart
  - Set order item status to "paid"
- Shipping address snapshot stored with order
- Transaction atomicity: all or nothing

## Order Status Management
- Order item statuses: paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded
- Order status derived from items:
  - All paid → "paid"
  - Any shipped, none delivered → "shipped"
  - All delivered → "delivered"
  - All cancelled → "cancelled"
  - All refunded → "refunded"
  - Mixed → "partially_completed"
- Status recalculation on any item status change

## Shipping & Tracking
- Shipment belongs to seller and order
- Shipment contains multiple order items (same seller only)
- Tracking info: carrier_name, tracking_number
- Shipment creation sets items to "shipped"
- Customer delivery confirmation sets items to "delivered"
- Auto-delivery: 14 days after shipping if not confirmed

## Order Cancellation
- Customer requests cancellation for "paid" items only
- Cancellation request stores reason, status (pending, approved, rejected)
- Seller approves/rejects with snapshot of state change
- Approval: item status → "cancelled", create positive inventory record
- Rejection: request status → "rejected", item unchanged
- Snapshots track all state changes

## Refund Requests
- Customer requests refund for "delivered" items only
- Validation: within 7 days of delivery
- Refund request stores reason, status (pending, approved, rejected)
- Seller approves/rejects with snapshot of state change
- Approval: item status → "refunded", create positive inventory record
- Rejection: request status → "rejected", item unchanged
- Snapshots track all state changes

## Review & Rating System
- Review creation: customer, product, order_item, rating (1-5), optional text
- Validation: item status must be "delivered", one review per product per order
- Review editing creates snapshot
- Review deletion: soft delete (deleted_at), preserved for historical accuracy
- Average rating: AVG of non-deleted reviews
- Reviews displayed on product detail page

## Seller Dashboard
- Shop summary: COUNT products, COUNT order_items, COUNT pending cancellations, COUNT pending refunds
- Order items list filtered by seller's products
- Status filtering support

## Administrator System
- Admin request: user submits reason, status pending
- Super admin approve/reject: approved → regular admin
- Grade management: super admin can promote/demote others (not self)
- Seller management: approve, reject (with reason), suspend, unsuspend
- Suspended sellers: products hidden, cannot create/edit products, can process existing orders
- Customer management: ban/unban (banned cannot login)
- Seller ban: cannot login, existing orders remain
- Product oversight: view all, delete any (policy violations)
- Order oversight: force-cancel, force-refund (bypasses normal workflow)

## Snapshot System Implementation
- Snapshots are immutable append-only records
- Product snapshot: captures all product fields + all variant snapshots at that moment
- Variant snapshot: captures SKU, options, price
- Seller profile snapshot: shop name, description, logo
- Order item snapshot: product name, description, variant options, price at purchase
- Seller profile snapshot in order: shop name, logo at purchase
- Review snapshot: rating, text
- Cancellation/refund snapshot: reason, status changes
- All snapshots include: created_at, before_values, after_values, changed_by
- Queryable by owners and administrators

## Access Control & Permissions
- Customers: access own profile, addresses, wishlist, cart, orders, reviews
- Sellers: access own products, variants, inventory, order items, dashboard
- Admins: access all data with grade-based restrictions
- Super admins: full access including admin management
- Validate ownership on all update/delete operations
- Check seller approval status before allowing product operations
- Check seller suspension status (suspended cannot create/edit products)

## Data Integrity & Validation
- Email uniqueness for customers and sellers (separate namespaces or unified)
- SKU uniqueness per product
- Foreign key constraints with appropriate cascade rules
- Transaction management for multi-step operations
- Optimistic locking where appropriate
- Input validation on all DTOs
- Business rule validation in service layer
